[AWS::ObservabilityAdmin::OrganizationCentralizationRule](../UserGuide/aws-resource-organizationcentralizationrule.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-organizationcentralizationrule.md") Use the `AWS::ObservabilityAdmin::OrganizationCentralizationRule` resource to define how telemetry data should be centralized across an organization, including source and destination configurations. [AWS::ObservabilityAdmin::OrganizationTelemetryRule](../UserGuide/aws-resource-observabilityadmin-organizationtelemetryrule.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-observabilityadmin-organizationtelemetryrule.md") Use the `AWS::ObservabilityAdmin::OrganizationTelemetryRule` resource to retrieve the details of a specific organization centralization rule. This operation can only be called by the organization's management account or a delegated administrator account. [AWS::ObservabilityAdmin::TelemetryRule](../UserGuide/aws-resource-telemetryrule.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-telemetryrule.md") Use the `AWS::ObservabilityAdmin::TelemetryRule` resource to create a telemetry rule that defines how telemetry should be configured forAWS resources in your account. The rule specifies which resources should have telemetry enabled and how that telemetry data should be collected based on resource type, telemetry type, and selection criteria. | [Updated resource](aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_PCS "aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_PCS")                                                                                                          | The following resource was updated: AWS::PCS::ComputeNodeGroup. [AWS::PCS::ComputeNodeGroup](../UserGuide/aws-resource-pcs-computenodegroup.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-pcs-computenodegroup.md") Added support for Amazon EC2 Capacity Blocks for ML as an option for AWS PCS compute node groups to purchase and launch instances. Specify `CAPACITY_BLOCK` as the `PurchaseOption` for your compute node group. The launch template for the compute node group must also be configured to use Capacity Blocks. For more information, see [Using Amazon EC2 Capacity Blocks for ML with AWS PCS](../../../pcs/latest/userguide/capacity-blocks.md "../../../pcs/latest/userguide/capacity-blocks.md") in the _AWS PCS User Guide_. | [New resources](aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_SMSVOICE "aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_SMSVOICE")                                                                                                   | The following resources were added: `AWS::SMSVOICE::ConfigurationSet`, `AWS::SMSVOICE::OptOutList`, `AWS::SMSVOICE::PhoneNumber`, `AWS::SMSVOICE::Pool`, `ProtectConfiguration`, `AWS::SMSVOICE::ResourcePolicy` and `AWS::SMSVOICE::SenderId`. [AWS::SMSVOICE::ConfigurationSet](aws-resource-smsvoice-configurationset.md "aws-resource-smsvoice-configurationset.md") Use the `AWS::SMSVOICE::ConfigurationSet` resource to specify a set of rules that are applied when you send a message. [AWS::SMSVOICE::OptOutList](aws-resource-smsvoice-optoutlist.md "aws-resource-smsvoice-optoutlist.md") Use the `AWS::SMSVOICE::OptOutList` resource to specify a list of destination phone numbers that should not have messages sent to them. [AWS::SMSVOICE::PhoneNumber](aws-resource-smsvoice-phonenumber.md "aws-resource-smsvoice-phonenumber.md") Use the `AWS::SMSVOICE::PhoneNumber` resource to create specify a phone number that your recipients see on their devices when you send them an SMS or MMS message. [AWS::SMSVOICE::Pool](aws-resource-smsvoice-pool.md "aws-resource-smsvoice-pool.md") Use the `AWS::SMSVOICE::Pool` resource to create a new pool, which is a collection of phone numbers or sender IDs that share the same settings that you can use to send messages. [AWS::SMSVOICE::ProtectConfiguration](aws-resource-smsvoice-protectconfiguration.md "aws-resource-smsvoice-protectconfiguration.md") Use the `AWS::SMSVOICE::ProtectConfiguration` resource to create a set of capabilities to manage SMS deliveries to all countries where your customers are located. [AWS::SMSVOICE::ResourcePolicy](aws-resource-smsvoice-resourcepolicy.md "aws-resource-smsvoice-resourcepolicy.md") Use the `AWS::SMSVOICE::ResourcePolicy` resource to specify the permissions for another AWS account on a shared resource. [AWS::SMSVOICE::SenderId](aws-resource-smsvoice-senderid.md "aws-resource-smsvoice-senderid.md") Use the `AWS::SMSVOICE::SenderId` resource to request a new sender ID that doesn't require You can configure either multi-Region eventual consistency (MREC) or multi-Region strong consistency (MRSC). [AWS::DynamoDB::GlobalTable GlobalTableWitnesses](../UserGuide/aws-properties-dynamodb-globaltable-globaltablewitnesses.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-dynamodb-globaltable-globaltablewitnesses.md") Use this property to configure witnesses for MRSC global tables. A witness Region enhances availability for MRSC global tables in a two-replica configuration by providing an additional voting member without storing data. [AWS::DynamoDB::GlobalTable GlobalTableWitness](../UserGuide/aws-properties-dynamodb-globaltable-globaltablewitness.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-dynamodb-globaltable-globaltablewitness.md") Use this property to specify the witness Region for an MRSC global table. The witness must be in a different Region than the replicas and within the same Region set. In the property type `InternalAccessConfiguration`, use the property `InternalAccessAnalysisRule` to specify analysis rules for the internal access analyzer. Only the credentials from the target IAM role are put into the pod. The target role can be from another account, unlike the association role. Use the `DisableSessionTags` property to enable or disable the session tags that are added by EKS Pod Identity and lower the number of tags to stay under the session size limit. Use the `ExternalId` return value in an IAM trust policy on the target IAM role to prevent the confused deputy problem. | [Updated resources](aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_CleanRooms "aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_CleanRooms")                                                                                           | The following resources were updated: `AWS::CleanRooms::AnalysisTemplate`, `AWS::CleanRooms::Collaboration`, `AWS::CleanRooms::Membership`, and `AWS::CleanRooms::ConfiguredTable`. [AWS::CleanRooms::AnalysisTemplate](../UserGuide/aws-resource-cleanrooms-analysistemplate.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-cleanrooms-analysistemplate.md") Use the `AnalysisTemplateArtifacts` property to specify the entry point and additional artifacts for the analysis template. Use the `SourceMetadata` property to specify the source metadata for the analysis template. Use the `Schema` property to specify the entire schema object for the analysis template. In the [Hash](../UserGuide/aws-properties-cleanrooms-analysistemplate-hash.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-cleanrooms-analysistemplate-hash.md") property type, use the `Sha256` property to specify the SHA-256 hash value. In the [S3Location](../UserGuide/aws-properties-cleanrooms-analysistemplate-s3location.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-cleanrooms-analysistemplate-s3location.md") property type, use the `Bucket` property to specify the bucket name and the `Key` property to specify the object key. mw [AWS::CleanRooms::Collaboration](../UserGuide/aws-resource-cleanrooms-collaboration.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-cleanrooms-collaboration.md") Use the `JobComputePaymentConfig` property to specify payment responsibilities for query and job compute costs. Use the `PaymentConfiguration` property to specify the compute configuration for the job. Use the `JobLogStatus` property to enable or disable job logging for the collaboration. In the [ProtectedJobS3OutputConfigurationInput](../UserGuide/aws-properties-cleanrooms-membership-protectedjobs3outputconfigurationinput.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-cleanrooms-membership-protectedjobs3outputconfigurationinput.md") property type, use the `Bucket` property to specify the S3 bucket for job output and the `KeyPrefix` property to specify the S3 prefix to unload the protected job results. [AWS::CleanRooms::Membership](../UserGuide/aws-resource-cleanrooms-membership.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-cleanrooms-membership.md") Use the `MembershipProtectedJobResultConfiguration` property to specify configurations for protected job results. Use the `MembershipJobComputePaymentConfig` property to specify the payment responsibilities for job compute costs. Use the `DefaultJobResultConfiguration` property to specify the default job result configuration for the membership. Use the `JobLogStatus` property to enable or disable job logging for the membership. [AWS::CleanRooms::ConfiguredTable](../UserGuide/aws-resource-cleanrooms-configuredtable.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-cleanrooms-configuredtable.md") Use the `SelectedAnalysisMethods` property to specify the selected analysis methods for the configured table. [AWS::S3Express::AccessPoint](../UserGuide/aws-resource-s3express-accesspoint.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-s3express-accesspoint.md") Use the `AWS::S3Express::AccessPoint` resource to specify access points for directory buckets. Use the `Scope` property to filter access control to specific prefixes, API operations, or a combination of both for directory buckets. [AWS::GameLiftStreams::StreamGroup](../UserGuide/aws-resource-gameliftstreams-streamgroup.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-gameliftstreams-streamgroup.md") Use the `AWS::GameLiftStreams::StreamGroup` resource to specify a stream group. | [New resources](aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_Bedrock "aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_Bedrock")                                                                                                     | The following resources were added: `AWS::Bedrock::Prompt`, `AWS::Bedrock::PromptVersion`, `AWS::Bedrock::Flow`, `AWS::Bedrock::FlowVersion`, and `AWS::Bedrock::FlowAlias`. [AWS::Bedrock::Prompt](../UserGuide/aws-resource-bedrock-prompt.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-bedrock-prompt.md") Use the `AWS::Bedrock::Prompt` resource to create a prompt in Amazon Bedrock to reuse in different workflows. For more information, see [Construct and store reusable prompts with Prompt management in Amazon Bedrock](../../../bedrock/latest/userguide/prompt-management.md "../../../bedrock/latest/userguide/prompt-management.md"). [AWS::Bedrock::PromptVersion](../UserGuide/aws-resource-bedrock-promptversion.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-bedrock-promptversion.md") Use the `AWS::Bedrock::PromptVersion` resource to create a version of your prompt that acts as a static snapshot of a prompt configuration. For more information, see [Construct and store reusable prompts with Prompt management in Amazon Bedrock](../../../bedrock/latest/userguide/prompt-management.md "../../../bedrock/latest/userguide/prompt-management.md"). [AWS::Bedrock::Flow](../UserGuide/aws-resource-bedrock-flow.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-bedrock-flow.md") Use the `AWS::Bedrock::Flow` resource to create a prompt flow in Amazon Bedrock so that you can chain resources from Amazon Bedrock and other AWS services to create complex workflows that take advantage of generative AI. For more information, see [Build an end-to-end generative AI workflow with prompt flows in Amazon Bedrock](../../../bedrock/latest/userguide/prompt-flows.md "../../../bedrock/latest/userguide/prompt-flows.md"). [AWS::Bedrock::FlowVersion](../UserGuide/aws-resource-bedrock-flowversion.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-bedrock-flowversion.md") Use the `AWS::Bedrock::FlowVersion` resource to create a version of your prompt flow that acts as a static snapshot of a prompt flow. For more information, see [Build an end-to-end generative AI workflow with prompt flows in Amazon Bedrock](../../../bedrock/latest/userguide/prompt-flows.md "../../../bedrock/latest/userguide/prompt-flows.md"). [AWS::Bedrock::FlowAlias](../UserGuide/aws-resource-bedrock-flowalias.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-bedrock-flowalias.md") Use the `AWS::Bedrock::FlowAlias` resource to create an alias of your prompt flow that points to a version of the prompt flow. For more information, see [Build an end-to-end generative AI workflow with prompt flows in Amazon Bedrock](../../../bedrock/latest/userguide/prompt-flows.md "../../../bedrock/latest/userguide/prompt-flows.md"). | [New resources](aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_SES "aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_SES")                                                                                                             | The following resources were added: `AWS::SES::MailManagerAddonInstance`, `AWS::SES::MailManagerAddonSubscription`, `AWS::SES::MailManagerArchive`, `AWS::SES::MailManagerIngressPoint`, `AWS::SES::MailManagerRelay`, `AWS::SES::MailManagerRuleSet`, and `AWS::SES::MailManagerTrafficPolicy`. [`AWS::SES::MailManagerAddonInstance`](aws-resource-ses-mailmanageraddoninstance.md "aws-resource-ses-mailmanageraddoninstance.md") Use the `AWS::SES::MailManagerAddonInstance` resource to create an Add On instance which represents the actual deployment and configuration of the Add On functionality within your Mail Manager environment. [`AWS::SES::MailManagerAddonSubscription`](aws-resource-ses-mailmanageraddonsubscription.md "aws-resource-ses-mailmanageraddonsubscription.md") Use the `AWS::SES::MailManagerAddonSubscription` resource to create an Add On subscription which represents the acceptance of the Add On's terms of use and any additional pricing. [`AWS::SES::MailManagerArchive`](aws-resource-ses-mailmanagerarchive.md "aws-resource-ses-mailmanagerarchive.md") Use the `AWS::SES::MailManagerArchive` resource to create a new email archive resource for storing and retaining emails. [`AWS::SES::MailManagerIngressPoint`](aws-resource-ses-mailmanageringresspoint.md "aws-resource-ses-mailmanageringresspoint.md") Use the `AWS::SES::MailManagerIngressPoint` resource to provision an ingress endpoint which serves as the entry point for incoming emails, allowing you to define how emails are received and processed within your AWS environment. [`AWS::SES::MailManagerRelay`](aws-resource-ses-mailmanagerrelay.md "aws-resource-ses-mailmanagerrelay.md") Use the `AWS::SES::MailManagerRelay` resource to create an SMTP relay which can be used within a Mail Manager rule set to forward incoming emails to defined relay destinations. [`AWS::SES::MailManagerRuleSet`](aws-resource-ses-mailmanagerruleset.md "aws-resource-ses-mailmanagerruleset.md") Use the `AWS::SES::MailManagerRuleSet` resource to create a rule set for a Mail Manager ingress endpoint which contains a list of rules that are evaluated sequentially for each email. [`AWS::SES::MailManagerTrafficPolicy`](aws-resource-ses-mailmanagertrafficpolicy.md "aws-resource-ses-mailmanagertrafficpolicy.md") Use the `AWS::SES::MailManagerTrafficPolicy` resource to create a traffic policy for a Mail Manager ingress endpoint which contains policy statements used to evaluate whether incoming emails should be allowed or denied. `AWS::SecurityHub::PolicyAssociation` resource to associate a Security Hub configuration policy or self-managed configuration with the organization root, an account, or an organizational unit (OU). | [New resources](aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_QBusiness "aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_QBusiness")                                                                                                 | The following resources were added: `AWS::QBusiness::Application`, `AWS::QBusiness::DataSource`, `AWS::QBusiness::Index`, `AWS::QBusiness::Plugin`, `AWS::QBusiness::Retriever`, and `AWS::QBusiness::WebExperience`. [AWS::QBusiness::Application](../UserGuide/aws-resource-qbusiness-application.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-qbusiness-application.md") Use the `AWS::QBusiness::Application` resource to create an Amazon Q Business application. For more information, see [Configuring an Amazon Q Business application](../../../amazonq/latest/qbusiness-ug/create-application.md "../../../amazonq/latest/qbusiness-ug/create-application.md"). [AWS::QBusiness::DataSource](../UserGuide/aws-resource-qbusiness-datasource.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-qbusiness-datasource.md") Use the `AWS::QBusiness::DataSource` resource to create a data source connector for an Amazon Q Business application. For more information, see [Configuring Amazon Q Business data source connectors](../../../amazonq/latest/qbusiness-ug/supported-connectors.md "../../../amazonq/latest/qbusiness-ug/supported-connectors.md"). [AWS::QBusiness::Index](../UserGuide/aws-resource-qbusiness-index.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-qbusiness-index.md") Use the `AWS::QBusiness::Index` resource to create an Amazon Q Business index. For more information, see [Creating an Amazon Q Business index](../../../amazonq/latest/qbusiness-ug/native-retriever.md "../../../amazonq/latest/qbusiness-ug/native-retriever.md"). [AWS::QBusiness::Plugin](../UserGuide/aws-resource-qbusiness-plugin.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-qbusiness-plugin.md") Use the `AWS::QBusiness::Plugin` resource to create and configure an Amazon Q Business plugin. For more information, see [Configuring plugins with Amazon Q Business](../../../amazonq/latest/qbusiness-ug/plugins.md "../../../amazonq/latest/qbusiness-ug/plugins.md"). [AWS::QBusiness::Retriever](../UserGuide/aws-resource-qbusiness-retriever.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-qbusiness-retriever.md") Use the `AWS::QBusiness::Retriever` resource to add a retriever to an Amazon Q Business application. For more information, see [Selecting a retriever for Amazon Q Business](../../../amazonq/latest/qbusiness-ug/select-retriever.md "../../../amazonq/latest/qbusiness-ug/select-retriever.md"). [AWS::QBusiness::WebExperience](../UserGuide/aws-resource-qbusiness-webexperience.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-qbusiness-webexperience.md") Use the `AWS::QBusiness::WebExperience` resource to create an Amazon Q Business web experience. For more information, see [Customizing an Amazon Q Business web experience](../../../amazonq/latest/qbusiness-ug/customizing-web-experience.md "../../../amazonq/latest/qbusiness-ug/customizing-web-experience.md") . [AWS::WorkSpacesWeb::BrowserSettings](../UserGuide/aws-resource-workspacesweb-browsersettings.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-workspacesweb-browsersettings.md") Use the `AdditionalEncryptionContext` property to specify the additional encryption context of the browser settings. Use the `CustomerManagedKey` property to specify the custom managed key of the browser settings. [AWS::WorkSpacesWeb::IpAccessSettings](../UserGuide/aws-resource-workspacesweb-ipaccesssettings.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-workspacesweb-ipaccesssettings.md") Use the `AdditionalEncryptionContext` property to specify the additional encryption context of the IP access settings. Use the `CustomerManagedKey` property to specify the custom managed key of the IP access settings. [AWS::WorkSpacesWeb::Portal](../UserGuide/aws-resource-workspacesweb-portal.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-workspacesweb-portal.md") Use the `AdditionalEncryptionContext` property to specify the additional encryption context of the portal. Use the `CustomerManagedKey` property to specify the custom managed key of the portal. Use the `InstanceType` property to specify the type and resources of the underlying instance. Use the `MaxConcurrentSessions` property to specify the maximum number of concurrent sessions for the portal. [AWS::WorkSpacesWeb::UserSettings](../UserGuide/aws-resource-workspacesweb-usersettings.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-workspacesweb-usersettings.md") Use the `AdditionalEncryptionContext` property to specify the additional encryption context of the user settings. Use the `CustomerManagedKey` property to specify the custom managed key of the user settings. | [New resources](aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_Bedrock "aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_Bedrock")                                                                                                     | The following resources were added: `AWS::Bedrock::Agent`, `AWS::Bedrock::AgentAlias`, `AWS::Bedrock::KnowledgeBase`, and `AWS::Bedrock::DataSource`. [AWS::Bedrock::Agent](../UserGuide/aws-resource-bedrock-agent.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-bedrock-agent.md") Use the `AWS::Bedrock::Agent` resource to create an agent in Amazon Bedrock to help users fulfill tasks. For more information, see [Automate tasks in your application using conversational agents](../../../bedrock/latest/userguide/agents.md "../../../bedrock/latest/userguide/agents.md"). [AWS::Bedrock::AgentAlias](../UserGuide/aws-resource-bedrock-agentalias.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-bedrock-agentalias.md") Use the `AWS::Bedrock::AgentAlias` resource to create an alias that points to a version of your Amazon Bedrock agent that your application can invoke during deployment. For more information, see [Deploy an Amazon Bedrock Agent](../../../bedrock/latest/userguide/agents-deploy.md "../../../bedrock/latest/userguide/agents-deploy.md"). [AWS::Bedrock::KnowledgeBase](../UserGuide/aws-resource-bedrock-knowledgebase.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-bedrock-knowledgebase.md") Use the `AWS::Bedrock::KnowledgeBase` resource to create a knowledge base in Amazon Bedrock that can be queried and generate responses based on the retrieved results. For more information, see [Retrieve data and generate AI responses with knowledge bases](../../../bedrock/latest/userguide/knowledge-base.md "../../../bedrock/latest/userguide/knowledge-base.md") . [AWS::Bedrock::DataSource](../UserGuide/aws-resource-bedrock-datasource.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-bedrock-datasource.md") Use the `AWS::Bedrock::DataSource` resource to create a data source in a knowledge base in Amazon Bedrock to manage the conversion of data from an Amazon S3 bucket into vector embeddings for a knowledge base. For more information, see [Set up a data source for your knowledge base](../../../bedrock/latest/userguide/knowledge-base-ds.md "../../../bedrock/latest/userguide/knowledge-base-ds.md") . [AWS::SecurityHub::DelegatedAdmin](../UserGuide/aws-resource-securityhub-delegatedadmin.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-securityhub-delegatedadmin.md") Use the `AWS::SecurityHub::DelegatedAdmin` resource to specify the delegated Security Hub administrator for an organization. [AWS::SecurityHub::Insight](../UserGuide/aws-resource-securityhub-insight.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-securityhub-insight.md") Use the `AWS::SecurityHub::Insight` resource to specify a custom Security Hub insight. | [New resources](aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_Deadline "aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_Deadline")                                                                                                   | The following resources were added: [AWS::Deadline::Farm](../UserGuide/aws-resource-deadline-farm.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-deadline-farm.md") Use the AWS::Deadline::Farm resource to create a farm that contains the queues and fleets that process you jobs. For more information, see [AWS Deadline Cloud farms](../../../deadline-cloud/latest/userguide/farms.md "../../../deadline-cloud/latest/userguide/farms.md"). [AWS::Deadline::Fleet](../UserGuide/aws-resource-deadline-fleet.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-deadline-fleet.md") Use the AWS::Deadline::Fleet resource to define a fleet of worker hosts that process the tasks for your jobs. For more information, see [Manage AWS Deadline Cloud fleets](../../../deadline-cloud/latest/userguide/manage-fleets.md "../../../deadline-cloud/latest/userguide/manage-fleets.md"). [AWS::Deadline::LicenseEndpoint](../UserGuide/aws-resource-deadline-licenseendpoint.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-deadline-licenseendpoint.md") Use the AWS::Deadline::LicenseEndpoint resource to integrate licensed software with your jobs. For more information, see [Connect customer-managed fleets to a license endpoint](../../../deadline-cloud/latest/userguide/cmf-ubl.md "../../../deadline-cloud/latest/userguide/cmf-ubl.md"). [AWS::Deadline::MeteredProduct](../UserGuide/aws-resource-deadline-meteredproduct.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-deadline-meteredproduct.md") Use the AWS::Deadline::MeteredProduct resource to associate a licensed application with a license endpoint. [AWS::Deadline::Queue](../UserGuide/aws-resource-deadline-queue.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-deadline-queue.md") Use the AWS::Deadline::Queue resource to create queues for your farm. Jobs are submitted to a queue, and the queue sends the tasks in the job to a worker fleet for processing. For more information, see [Queues](../../../deadline-cloud/latest/userguide/queues.md "../../../deadline-cloud/latest/userguide/queues.md"). [AWS::Deadline::QueueEnvironment](../UserGuide/aws-resource-deadline-queueenvironment.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-deadline-queueenvironment.md") Use the AWS::Deadline::QueueEnvironment resource to create to create a processing environment for workers processing tasks from the queue. For more information, see [Create a queue environment](../../../deadline-cloud/latest/userguide/queues.md#create-queue-environment "../../../deadline-cloud/latest/userguide/queues.md#create-queue-environment"). [AWS::Deadline::QueueFleetAssociation](../UserGuide/aws-resource-deadline-queuefleetassociation.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-deadline-queuefleetassociation.md") Use the AWS::Deadline::QueueFleetAssociation resource to associate a worker fleet with a queue. Workers in the fleet process tasks for the jobs in the queue. For more information, see [Associate a queue and fleet](../../../deadline-cloud/latest/userguide/queues.md#associate-a-queue-and-fleet "../../../deadline-cloud/latest/userguide/queues.md#associate-a-queue-and-fleet"). [AWS::Deadline::StorageProfile](../UserGuide/aws-resource-deadline-storageprofile.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-deadline-storageprofile.md") Use the AWS::Deadline::StorageProfile resource to specify the operating system, file type, and file location of resources used by a farm. For more information, see [Storage profiles in AWS Deadline Cloud](../../../deadline-cloud/latest/userguide/storage-shared.md#storage-profile "../../../deadline-cloud/latest/userguide/storage-shared.md#storage-profile") . | [New resource](aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_DataZone "aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_DataZone")                                                                                                    | The following resources were added: `AWS::DataZone::DataSource`, `AWS::DataZone::Domain`, `AWS::DataZone::Environment`, `AWS::DataZone::EnvironmentBlueprintConfiguration`, `AWS::DataZone::EnvironmentProfile`, `AWS::DataZone::Project`, `AWS::DataZone::SubscriptionTarget`. [AWS::DataZone::DataSource](../UserGuide/aws-resource-datazone-datasource.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-datazone-datasource.md") Use the `AWS::DataZone::DataSource` resource to specify an Amazon DataZone data source that is used to import technical metadata of assets (data) from the source databases or data warehouses into Amazon DataZone. [AWS::DataZone::Domain](../UserGuide/aws-resource-datazone-domain.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-datazone-domain.md") Use the `AWS::DataZone::Domain` resource to specify an Amazon DataZone domain. You can use domains to organize your assets, users, and their projects. [AWS::DataZone::Environment](../UserGuide/aws-resource-datazone-environment.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-datazone-environment.md") Use the `AWS::DataZone::Environment` resource to specify an Amazon DataZone environment, which is a collection of zero or more configured resources with a given set of IAM principals who can operate on those resources. [AWS::DataZone::EnvironmentBlueprintConfiguration](../UserGuide/aws-resource-datazone-environmentblueprintconfiguration.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-datazone-environmentblueprintconfiguration.md") Use the `AWS::DataZone::EnvironmentBlueprintConfiguration` resource to specify the configuration details of an environment blueprint. [AWS::DataZone::EnvironmentProfile](../UserGuide/aws-resource-datazone-environmentprofile.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-datazone-environmentprofile.md") Use the `AWS::DataZone::EnvironmentProfile` resource to specify the details of an environment profile. [AWS::DataZone::Project](../UserGuide/aws-resource-datazone-project.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-datazone-project.md") Use the `AWS::DataZone::Project` resource to specify an Amazon DataZone project. Projects enable a group of users to collaborate on various business use cases that involve publishing, discovering, subscribing to, and consuming data in the Amazon DataZone catalog. Project members consume assets from the Amazon DataZone catalog and produce new assets using one or more analytical workflows. [AWS::DataZone::SubscriptionTarget](../UserGuide/aws-resource-datazone-subscriptiontarget.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-datazone-subscriptiontarget.md") Use the `AWS::DataZone::SubscriptionTarget` resource to specify an Amazon DataZone subscription target. Subscription targets enable you to access the data to which you have subscribed in your projects. A subscription target specifies the location (for example, a database or a schema) and the required permissions (for example, an IAM role) that Amazon DataZone can use to establish a connection with the source data and to create the necessary grants so that members of the Amazon DataZone project can start querying the data to which they have subscribed. The federation role must exist in your account and provide the [required minimum permissions](../../../awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/query-federation.md#query-federation-permissions-role [AWS::WorkSpacesWeb::UserAccessLoggingSettings](../UserGuide/aws-resource-workspacesweb-useraccessloggingsettings.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-workspacesweb-useraccessloggingsettings.md") Use the `AWS::WorkSpacesWeb::UserAccessLoggingSettings` resource to specify user access logging settings that can be associated with a web portal. [AWS::WorkSpacesWeb::UserSettings](../UserGuide/aws-resource-workspacesweb-usersettings.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-workspacesweb-usersettings.md") Use the `AWS::WorkSpacesWeb::UserSettings` resource to specify user settings that can be associated with a web portal. [AWS::WAFv2::WebACL](../UserGuide/aws-resource-wafv2-webacl.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-wafv2-webacl.md") Use the `AWSManagedRulesACFPRuleSet` property to configure your use of the account creation fraud prevention (ACFP) managed rule group, in a managed rule group reference statement. For protected CloudFront distributions, in addition to inspecting account registration and account creation requests, you can also use ACFP to block new account creation attempts from clients that have recently submitted too many failed account creation attempts. The following resource was added: AWS::SecurityHub::Standard. [AWS::SecurityHub::Hub](../UserGuide/aws-resource-securityhub-hub.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-securityhub-hub.md") Use the `AutoEnableControls` property to specify whether you want Security Hub to automatically enable new controls as they are added to your enabled standards. For more information, see [Enabling new controls in enabled standards automatically](../../../securityhub/latest/userguide/controls-auto-enable.md "../../../securityhub/latest/userguide/controls-auto-enable.md"). Use the `ControlFindingGenerator` property to specify whether you want Security Hub to generate a single finding or separate findings when a control applies to multiple standards. For more information, see [Consolidated control findings](../../../securityhub/latest/userguide/controls-findings-create-update.md#consolidated-control-findings "../../../securityhub/latest/userguide/controls-findings-create-update.md#consolidated-control-findings"). Use the `EnableDefaultStandards` property to specify whether you want to enable security standards that Security Hub has designated as default standards. For more information, see [Automatically enabled security standards](../../../securityhub/latest/userguide/securityhub-standards-enable-disable.md#securityhub-auto-enabled-standards "../../../securityhub/latest/userguide/securityhub-standards-enable-disable.md#securityhub-auto-enabled-standards"). [AWS::SecurityHub::Standard](../UserGuide/aws-resource-securityhub-standard.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-securityhub-standard.md") Use the `AWS::SecurityHub::Standard` resource to enable a specified security standard in Security Hub. [AWS::MediaConnect::Bridge](../UserGuide/aws-resource-mediaconnect-bridge.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-mediaconnect-bridge.md") Use the `AWS::MediaConnect::Bridge` resource to create a connection between your data center instance and the cloud. [AWS::MediaConnect::BridgeOutput](../UserGuide/aws-resource-mediaconnect-bridgeoutput.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-mediaconnect-bridgeoutput.md") Use the `AWS::MediaConnect::BridgeOutput` resource to add new outputs to an existing bridge. [AWS::MediaConnect::BridgeSource](../UserGuide/aws-resource-mediaconnect-bridgesource.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-mediaconnect-bridgesource.md") Use the `AWS::MediaConnect::BridgeSource` resource to add new sources to an existing bridge. The gateway is a logical grouping of Instances and Bridges. Each gateway utilizes user-defined IP information for communication between data centers and the cloud. | [New resource](aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_RDS "aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_RDS")                                                                                                              | The following resource was added: AWS::RDS::CustomDBEngineVersion [AWS::RDS::CustomDBEngineVersion](../UserGuide/aws-resource-rds-customdbengineversion.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-rds-customdbengineversion.md") The `DatabaseInstallationFilesS3BucketName` property is the name of an Amazon S3 bucket that contains database installation files for your CEV. The `DatabaseInstallationFilesS3Prefix` property is the Amazon S3 directory that contains the database installation files for your CEV. Use the `Description` property to provide an optional description of your CEV. Use the `Engine` property to indicate the database engine to use for your custom engine version (CEV). Use the `EngineVersion` property to indicate the name of your CEV in the format `19.customized_string`. Use the `KMSKeyId` property for the AWS KMS key identifier for an encrypted CEV. The `Manifest` property is the CEV manifest, which is a JSON document that describes the installation .zip files stored in Amazon S3. The `Status` property provides the status of a custom engine version (CEV). The `Tags` property allows you to add metadata to your RDS resource. [AWS::Shield::DRTAccess](../UserGuide/aws-resource-shield-drtaccess.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-shield-drtaccess.md") Use the `AWS::Shield::DRTAccess` resource to give permissions to the Shield response team (SRT) to access your account and your resource protections. This permits them to help you mitigate distributed denial of service (DDoS) attacks. [AWS::Shield::ProactiveEngagement](../UserGuide/aws-resource-shield-proactiveengagement.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-shield-proactiveengagement.md") Use the `AWS::Shield::ProactiveEngagement` resource to enable and disable authorization for the the Shield Response Team (SRT) to contact you and to initiate proactive support for potential attacks. [AWS::Shield::Protection](../UserGuide/aws-resource-shield-protection.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-shield-protection.md") Use the `AWS::Shield::Protection` resource to enable Shield Advanced protections for a specific AWS resource. [AWS::Shield::ProtectionGroup](../UserGuide/aws-resource-shield-protectiongroup.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-shield-protectiongroup.md") Use the `AWS::Shield::ProtectionGroup` resource to combine the management of selected protected resources, to improve the accuracy of detection and reduce false positives. Compatible mode allows your Valkey or Redis OSS clients to connect using both cluster mode enabled and cluster mode disabled. After you migrate all clients to use cluster mode enabled, you can then complete cluster mode configuration and set the cluster mode to Enabled. For more information, see [Modify cluster mode](../../../AmazonElastiCache/latest/dg/modify-cluster-mode.md "../../../AmazonElastiCache/latest/dg/modify-cluster-mode.md"). [AWS::MSK::Cluster](../UserGuide/aws-resource-msk-cluster.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-msk-cluster.md") Use the `VpcConnectivity` property to specify VPC connection control settings for brokers. Use the `VpcConnectivityClientAuthentication` property to get all client authentication information for VpcConnectivity. Use the `VpcConnectivitySasl` property to get details for SASL client authentication for VpcConnectivity. Use the `VpcConnectivityIam` property to get details for IAM client authentication for VpcConnectivity. Use the `VpcConnectivity.Iam.Enabled` property get details about whether IAM authentication is on or off. Use the `VpcConnectivityTls` property to get details for TLS client authentication for VpcConnectivity. Use the `VpcConnectivityTls.Enabled` property get details about whether TLS authentication is on or off. Use the `VpcConnectivityScram` property to get details for SCRAM client authentication for VpcConnectivity. Use the `VpcConnectivityScram.Enabled` property get details about whether SCRAM authentication is on or off. Use the `ConnectivityInfo.VpcConnectivity` property to get details for VPC connection control settings for brokers. | [New resources](aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_VpcLattice "aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_VpcLattice")                                                                                               | The following resources were added: AWS::VpcLattice::AccessLogSubscription, AWS::VpcLattice::AuthPolicy, AWS::VpcLattice::Listener, AWS::VpcLattice::ResourcePolicy, AWS::VpcLattice::Rule, AWS::VpcLattice::Service, AWS::VpcLattice::ServiceNetwork, AWS::VpcLattice::ServiceNetworkServiceAssociation, AWS::VpcLattice::ServiceNetworkVpcAssociation, AWS::VpcLattice::TargetGroup [AWS::VpcLattice::AccessLogSubscription](../UserGuide/aws-resource-vpclattice-accesslogsubscription.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-vpclattice-accesslogsubscription.md") Enables access logs to be sent to Amazon CloudWatch, Amazon S3, and Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose. [AWS::VpcLattice::AuthPolicy](../UserGuide/aws-resource-vpclattice-authpolicy.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-vpclattice-authpolicy.md") Creates or updates the auth policy. [AWS::VpcLattice::Listener](../UserGuide/aws-resource-vpclattice-listener.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-vpclattice-listener.md") Creates a listener for a service. [AWS::VpcLattice::ResourcePolicy](../UserGuide/aws-resource-vpclattice-resourcepolicy.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-vpclattice-resourcepolicy.md") Retrieves information about the resource policy. [AWS::VpcLattice::Rule](../UserGuide/aws-resource-vpclattice-rule.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-vpclattice-rule.md") Creates a listener rule. [AWS::VpcLattice::Service](../UserGuide/aws-resource-vpclattice-service.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-vpclattice-service.md") Creates a service. A service is any software application that can run on instances containers, or serverless functions within an account or virtual private cloud (VPC). [AWS::VpcLattice::ServiceNetwork](../UserGuide/aws-resource-vpclattice-servicenetwork.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-vpclattice-servicenetwork.md") Creates a service network. A service network is a logical boundary for a collection of services. [AWS::VpcLattice::ServiceNetworkServiceAssociation](../UserGuide/aws-resource-vpclattice-servicenetworkserviceassociation.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-vpclattice-servicenetworkserviceassociation.md") Associates a service with a service network. [AWS::VpcLattice::ServiceNetworkVpcAssociation](../UserGuide/aws-resource-vpclattice-servicenetworkvpcassociation.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-vpclattice-servicenetworkvpcassociation.md") Associates a VPC with a service network. [AWS::VpcLattice::TargetGroup](../UserGuide/aws-resource-vpclattice-targetgroup.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-vpclattice-targetgroup.md") Creates a target group. | [New resources](aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_CloudTrail "aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_CloudTrail")                                                                                               | The following new resources were added: AWS::CloudTrail::Channel and AWS::CloudTrail::ResourcePolicy [AWS::CloudTrail::Channel](../UserGuide/aws-resource-cloudtrail-channel.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-cloudtrail-channel.md") Use the `Channel` resource to specify a channel for logging events from outside AWS in CloudTrail Lake. Channels are used by partner event sources, or your custom event sources, to send events to CloudTrail Lake. For more information, see [Working with CloudTrail Lake](../../../awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/cloudtrail-lake.md "../../../awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/cloudtrail-lake.md") in the _AWS CloudTrail User Guide_. [AWS::CloudTrail::Channel.Channel](../UserGuide/aws-properties-cloudtrail-channel-channel.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-cloudtrail-channel-channel.md") Use the `Channel` property to specify the name and ARN of a channel that you use with integrations in CloudTrail Lake. For more information, see [Working with CloudTrail Lake](../../../awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/cloudtrail-lake.md "../../../awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/cloudtrail-lake.md") in the _AWS CloudTrail User Guide_. [AWS::CloudTrail::Channel.Destination](../UserGuide/aws-properties-cloudtrail-channel-destination.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-cloudtrail-channel-destination.md") Use the `Destination` property to specify destination event data stores for events that arrive over a channel in CloudTrail Lake. For more information, see [Working with CloudTrail Lake](../../../awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/cloudtrail-lake.md "../../../awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/cloudtrail-lake.md") in the _AWS CloudTrail User Guide_. [AWS::CloudTrail::ResourcePolicy](../UserGuide/aws-resource-cloudtrail-resourcepolicy.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-cloudtrail-resourcepolicy.md") Use the `ResourcePolicy` resource to attach a resource-based permission policy to a CloudTrail channel that is used for an integration with an event source outside of AWS. For more information about resource-based policies, see [CloudTrail resource-based policy examples](../../../awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/security_iam_resource-based-policy-examples.md "../../../awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/security_iam_resource-based-policy-examples.md") in the _CloudTrail User Guide_. [AWS::CloudTrail::ResourcePolicy.ResourceArn](../UserGuide/aws-properties-cloudtrail-resourcepolicy-resourcearn.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-cloudtrail-resourcepolicy-resourcearn.md") Use the `ResourceArn` property to specify the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the CloudTrail channel attached to the resource-based policy. The following is the format of a resource ARN: `arn:aws:cloudtrail:us-east-2:123456789012:channel/MyChannel`. [AWS::CloudTrail::ResourcePolicy.ResourcePolicy](../UserGuide/aws-properties-cloudtrail-resourcepolicy-resourcepolicy.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-cloudtrail-resourcepolicy-resourcepolicy.md") Use the `ResourcePolicy` property to specify the JSON-formatted string that contains the resource-based policy to attach to the CloudTrail channel. | [Updated resource](aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_Lex "aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_Lex")                                                                                                          | The following property type was updated: AWS::Lex::Bot. [AWS::Lex::Bot](../UserGuide/aws-resource-lex-bot.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-lex-bot.md") Use the [AllowedInputTypes](../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-allowedinputtypes.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-allowedinputtypes.md") property to specify the allowed input types. Use the [AudioSpecification](../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-audiospecification.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-audiospecification.md") property to specify the audio input specifications. Use the [AudioAndDTMFInputSpecification](../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-audioanddtmfinputspecification.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-audioanddtmfinputspecification.md") property to specify the audio and DTMF input specification. Use the [Condition](../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-condition.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-condition.md") property to provide an expression that evaluates to true or false. Use the [ConditionalBranch](../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-conditionalbranch.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-conditionalbranch.md") property to configure a set of actions that Amazon Lex should run if the condition is matched. Use the [ConditionalSpecification](../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-conditionalspecification.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-conditionalspecification.md") property to provide a list of conditional branches. Use the [DefaultConditionalBranch](../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-defaultconditionalbranch.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-defaultconditionalbranch.md") property to configure a set of actions that Amazon Lex should run if none of the other conditions are met. Use the [DialogAction](../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-dialogaction.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-dialogaction.md") property to define the action that the bot executes at runtime. Use the [DialogCodeHookInvocationSetting](../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-dialogcodehookinvocationsetting.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-dialogcodehookinvocationsetting.md") property to specify the dialog code hook that is called by Amazon Lex at a step of the conversation. Use the [DialogState](../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-dialogstate.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-dialogstate.md") property to configure the current state of the conversation with the user. Use the [DTMFSpecification](../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-dtmfspecification.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-dtmfspecification.md") property to specify the DTMF input specifications. Use the [ElicitationCodeHookInvocationSetting](../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-elicitationcodehookinvocationsetting.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-elicitationcodehookinvocationsetting.md") property to specify the dialog code hook that is called by Amazon Lex between eliciting slot values. Use the [InitialResponseSetting](../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-initialresponsesetting.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-initialresponsesetting.md") property to configure settings for a response sent to the user before Amazon Lex starts eliciting slots. Use the [Intent](../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-intent.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-intent.md") property to configure how Amazon Lex handles intents. Use the [IntentClosingSetting](../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-intentclosingsetting.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-intentclosingsetting.md") property to configure the statement that Amazon Lex conveys to the user when the intent is successfully fulfilled. Use the [IntentConfirmationSetting](../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-intentconfirmationsetting.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-intentconfirmationsetting.md") property to provide a prompt for making sure that the user is ready for the intent to be fulfilled. Use the [IntentOverride](../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-intentoverride.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-intentoverride.md") property to override settings to configure the intent state. Use the [PostDialogCodeHookInvocationSpecification](../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-postdialogcodehookinvocationspecification.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-postdialogcodehookinvocationspecification.md") property to specify next steps to run after the dialog code hook finishes. Use the [PostFulfillmentStatusSpecification](../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-postfulfillmentstatusspecification.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-postfulfillmentstatusspecification.md") property to configure the settings of the post-fulfillment response that is sent to the user. Use the [PromptAttemptSpecification](../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-promptattemptspecification.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-promptattemptspecification.md") property to specify the settings on a prompt attempt. Use the [PromptSpecification](../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-promptspecification.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-promptspecification.md") property to specify a list of message groups that Amazon Lex sends to a user to elicit a response. Use the [SessionAttribute](../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-sessionattribute.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-sessionattribute.md") property to specify session-specific context information. Use the [SlotCaptureSetting](../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-slotcapturesetting.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-slotcapturesetting.md") property to configure the settings that are used when Amazon Lex successfully captures a slot value from a user. Use the [SlotValue](../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-slotvalue.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-slotvalue.md") property to set values in a slot. Use the [SlotValueElicitationSetting](../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-slotvalueelicitationsetting.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-slotvalueelicitationsetting.md") property to specify the settings for eliciting a slot value. Use the [SlotValueOverride](../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-slotvalueoverride.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-slotvalueoverride.md") property to set slot values in a dialog step. Use the [SlotValueOverrideMap](../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-slotvalueoverridemap.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-slotvalueoverridemap.md") property to map slot names to a SlotValueOVerride object. Use the [TextInputSpecification](../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-textinputspecification.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-textinputspecification.md") property to specify the text input specifications. Use the [VoiceSettings](../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-voicesettings.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-voicesettings.md") property to specify the Amazon Polly voice used for audio interaction with the user.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | December 30, 2022  |

use the `Challenge` action. The following resource was updated: AWS ::Transfer::Server WorkflowDetails [AWS ::Transfer::Agreement](../UserGuide/aws-resource-transfer-agreement.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-transfer-agreement.md") Use the `Agreement` resource to specify an agreement between trading partners in AWS Transfer Family . [AWS ::Transfer::Certificate](../UserGuide/aws-resource-transfer-certificate.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-transfer-certificate.md") Use the `Certificate` resource to import signing and encryption certificates for AS2 in AWS Transfer Family . [AWS ::Transfer::Connector](../UserGuide/aws-resource-transfer-connector.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-transfer-connector.md") Use the `Connector` resource to create an entity that captures the parameters for an outbound AS2 connection in AWS Transfer Family . [AWS ::Transfer::Profile](../UserGuide/aws-resource-transfer-profile.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-transfer-profile.md") Use the `Profile` resource to specify local and partner profiles for servers in AWS Transfer Family that use the AS2 protocol. [AWS ::Transfer::Server WorkflowDetails](../UserGuide/aws-resource-transfer-server.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-transfer-server.md") Use the `OnPartialUpload` parameter to trigger a workflow in the case a transfer is interrupted and does not complete. The format is either `json_format` or `text_format`. Use the `JsonFormatRef` resource to represent object that represents the key value pairs for the JSON. Use the `LoggingFormat` resource to represent object that represents the format for the logs. [AWS::AppMesh::VirtualGateway](../UserGuide/aws-resource-appmesh-virtualgateway.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-appmesh-virtualgateway.md") Use the `VirtualGatewayFileAccessLogFormat` property to represent the specified format for the logs. The format is either `json_format` or `text_format`. Use the `JsonFormatRef` resource to represent object that represents the key value pairs for the JSON. Use the `LoggingFormat` resource to represent object that represents the format for the logs. [AWS::AppMesh::GatewayRoute](../UserGuide/aws-resource-appmesh-gatewayroute.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-appmesh-gatewayroute.md") Use the `Port` property to represent the port number of the gateway route target. [AWS::AppMesh::Route](../UserGuide/aws-resource-appmesh-route.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-appmesh-route.md") Use the `Port` property to represent the port number of the gateway route target. Use the `Port` property to represent an object that is the criteria for determining a request match. Use the `TcpRouteMatch` resource to represent an object that is the TCP route to match. [AWS::SES::EmailIdentity](aws-resource-ses-emailidentity.md "aws-resource-ses-emailidentity.md") Use the `EmailIdentity` resource to specify an identity, such as an email address or domain, for using within SES. [AWS::SES::EmailIdentity ConfigurationSetAttributes](aws-properties-ses-emailidentity-configurationsetattributes.md "aws-properties-ses-emailidentity-configurationsetattributes.md") Use the `ConfigurationSetAttributes` property to associate a configuration set with an email identity. [AWS::SES::EmailIdentity DkimAttributes](aws-properties-ses-emailidentity-dkimattributes.md "aws-properties-ses-emailidentity-dkimattributes.md") Use the `DkimAttributes` property to enable or disable DKIM authentication for an email identity. [AWS::SES::EmailIdentity DkimSigningAttributes](aws-properties-ses-emailidentity-dkimsigningattributes.md "aws-properties-ses-emailidentity-dkimsigningattributes.md") Use the `DkimSigningAttributes` property to configure or change the DKIM authentication settings for an email domain identity. [AWS::SES::EmailIdentity FeedbackAttributes](aws-properties-ses-emailidentity-feedbackattributes.md "aws-properties-ses-emailidentity-feedbackattributes.md") Use the `FeedbackAttributes` property to enable or disable feedback forwarding for an identity. [AWS::SES::EmailIdentity MailFromAttributes](aws-properties-ses-emailidentity-mailfromattributes.md "aws-properties-ses-emailidentity-mailfromattributes.md") Use the `MailFromAttributes` property to enable or disable the custom Mail-From domain configuration for an email identity. | [New resource](aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_CloudTrail "aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_CloudTrail")                                                                                                | The following resource was added: AWS::CloudTrail::EventDataStore [AWS::CloudTrail::EventDataStore](../UserGuide/aws-resource-cloudtrail-eventdatastore.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-cloudtrail-eventdatastore.md") Use the `EventDataStore` resource to specify an event data store in CloudTrail Lake. Event data stores are immutable collections of events based on criteria that you select by applying advanced event selectors. For more information, see [Working with CloudTrail Lake](../../../awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/cloudtrail-lake.md "../../../awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/cloudtrail-lake.md") in the _AWS CloudTrail User Guide_. [AWS::CloudTrail::EventDataStore.AdvancedEventSelector](../UserGuide/aws-properties-cloudtrail-eventdatastore-advancedeventselector.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-cloudtrail-eventdatastore-advancedeventselector.md") Use the `AdvancedEventSelector` property to specify fine-grained event properties for data events that you want to log to an event data store. For more information, see [Data events](../../../awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/logging-data-events-with-cloudtrail.md#logging-data-events "../../../awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/logging-data-events-with-cloudtrail.md#logging-data-events") in the _AWS CloudTrail User Guide_. [AWS::CloudTrail::EventDataStore.AdvancedFieldSelector](../UserGuide/aws-properties-cloudtrail-eventdatastore-advancedfieldselector.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-cloudtrail-eventdatastore-advancedfieldselector.md") Use the `AdvancedFieldSelector` property to specify fine-grained event properties for data events that you want to log to an event data store. An `AdvancedFieldSelector` is a single selector statement within an advanced event selector. For more information, see [Data events](../../../awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/logging-data-events-with-cloudtrail.md#logging-data-events "../../../awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/logging-data-events-with-cloudtrail.md#logging-data-events") in the _AWS CloudTrail User Guide_. [AWS::WAFv2::WebACL](../UserGuide/aws-resource-wafv2-webacl.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-wafv2-webacl.md") Use the `Cookies` property to specify that a rule statement should inspect the cookies in web requests. Use the `CookieMatchPattern` property to specify a subset of all cookies for inspection. Use the `Headers` property to specify that a rule statement should inspect the headers in web requests. Use the `HeaderMatchPattern` property to specify a subset of all headers for inspection. In the [Body](../UserGuide/aws-properties-wafv2-webacl-body.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-wafv2-webacl-body.md") property type, use the `OversizeHandling` property to specify how to handle web requests that have oversize body contents. In the [JsonBody](../UserGuide/aws-properties-wafv2-webacl-jsonbody.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-wafv2-webacl-jsonbody.md") property type, use the `OversizeHandling` property to specify how to handle web requests that have oversize body contents. [AWS::WAFv2::RuleGroup](../UserGuide/aws-resource-wafv2-rulegroup.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-wafv2-rulegroup.md") Use the `Cookies` property to specify that a rule statement should inspect the cookies in web requests. Use the `CookieMatchPattern` property to specify a subset of all cookies for inspection. Use the `Headers` property to specify that a rule statement should inspect the headers in web requests. Use the `HeaderMatchPattern` property to specify a subset of all headers for inspection. In the [Body](../UserGuide/aws-properties-wafv2-rulegroup-body.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-wafv2-rulegroup-body.md") property type, use the `OversizeHandling` property to specify how to handle web requests that have oversize body contents. In the [JsonBody](../UserGuide/aws-properties-wafv2-rulegroup-jsonbody.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-wafv2-rulegroup-jsonbody.md") property type, use the `OversizeHandling` property to specify how to handle web requests that have oversize body contents. [AWS::Lex::Bot](../UserGuide/aws-resource-lex-bot.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-lex-bot.md") Use the [AudioLogSetting](../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-audiologsetting.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-audiologsetting.md") property to configure logging of audio conversation with your users. Use the [AudioLogSetting](../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-botaliaslocalesettings.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-botaliaslocalesettings.md") property to configure the Lambda functions used for each of your bot's locales. Use the [ConversationLogsSettings](../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-conversationlogsettings.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-conversationlogsettings.md") property to manage logging that saves audio, text, and metadata of the conversations with your users. Use the [CustomVocabulary](../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-customvocabulary.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-customvocabulary.md") property to define custom vocabularies for your slot types. Use the [LambdaCodeHook](../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-lambdacodehook.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-lambdacodehook.md") property to specify a Lambda function that verifies requests to the bot or fulfills the user's request. Use the [S3BucketLogDestination](../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-s3bucketlogdestination.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-s3bucketlogdestination.md") property to configure the Amazon S3 bucket to hold audio conversation logs. Use the [SlotValueSelectionSetting](../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-slotvalueselectionsetting.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-slotvalueselectionsetting.md") property to configure advanced settings for recognizing slot values. Use the [TestBotAliasSettings](../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-testbotaliassettings.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-testbotaliassettings.md") property to configure the alias used for testing a bot. Use the [TextLogSetting](../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-textlogsetting.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-lex-bot-textlogsetting.md") property to configure text logs for conversations. | [New resource](aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_SSM "aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_SSM")                                                                                                              | The following resource was added: AWS::SSM::ResourcePolicy [AWS::SSM::ResourcePolicy](../UserGuide/aws-resource-ssm-document.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-ssm-document.md") Creates or updates a Systems Manager resource policy. A resource policy helps you to define the IAM entity (for example, an AWS account) that can manage your Systems Manager resources. Currently, `OpsItemGroup` is the only resource that supports Systems Manager resource policies. The resource policy for `OpsItemGroup` enables AWS accounts to view and interact with OpsCenter operational work items (OpsItems). OpsCenter is a tool in Systems Manager. For more information about OpsCenter, see [Systems Manager OpsCenter](../../../systems-manager/latest/userguide/OpsCenter.md "../../../systems-manager/latest/userguide/OpsCenter.md") in the Systems Manager User Guide. | [Updated resources](aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_SageMaker "aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_SageMaker")                                                                                             | The following resource was updated: AWS::SageMaker::Endpoint [AWS::SageMaker::Endpoint](../UserGuide/aws-resource-sagemaker-endpoint.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-sagemaker-endpoint.md") Use the `DeploymentConfig` property to specify the deployment configuration for an endpoint, which contains the desired deployment strategy and rollback configurations. Use the `AutoRollbackConfig` property to specify the the automatic rollback configuration for handling endpoint deployment failures and recovery. Use the `Alarm` property to specify a list of CloudWatch alarms that are configured to monitor metrics on an endpoint. Use the `AlarmName` property to specify the name of a CloudWatch alarm in your account. Use the `BlueGreenUpdatePolicy` property to specify the update policy for a blue/green deployment. Use the `MaximumExecutionTimeoutInSeconds` property to specify the maximum execution timeout for a blue/green deployment. Use the `TerminationWaitInSeconds` property to specify additional waiting time in seconds after the completion of an endpoint deployment before terminating the old endpoint fleet Use the `TrafficRoutingConfig` property to specify the traffic routing strategy during a blue/green endpoint deployment. Use the `CanarySize` property to specify the batch size for the first step to turn on traffic on the new endpoint fleet. Use the `LinearStepSize` property to specify the batch size for each step to turn on traffic on the new endpoint fleet Use the `Type` property to specify the traffic routing strategy type (all at once, canary, or linear). Use the `WaitIntervalInSeconds` property to specify the waiting time (in seconds) between incremental steps to turn on traffic on the new endpoint fleet. Use the `CapacitySize` property to specify the endpoint capacity to activate for production. Use the `Type` property to specify the endpoint capacity type to use (instance count or capacity percent). Use the `Value` property to specify the capacity size, either as a number of instances or a capacity percentage. Use the `RetainDeploymentConfig` property to specify whether to reuse the last deployment configuration. The default value is false (the configuration is not reused) | [New resources](aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_MemoryDB "aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_MemoryDB")                                                                                                   | The following resources were added: AWS::MemoryDB::Cluster, AWS::MemoryDB::ACL, AWS::MemoryDB::ParameterGroup, AWS::MemoryDB::SubnetGroup, and AWS::MemoryDB::User. [AWS::MemoryDB::Cluster](../UserGuide/aws-resource-memorydb-cluster.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-memorydb-cluster.md") Use the `Cluster` resource to specify a MemoryDBcluster. [AWS::MemoryDB::ACL](../UserGuide/aws-resource-memorydb-acl.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-memorydb-acl.md") Use the `ACL` resource to specify a MemoryDB access control list and associate it with a cluster. [AWS::MemoryDB::ParameterGroup](../UserGuide/aws-resource-memorydb-parametergroup.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-memorydb-parametergroup.md") Use the `ParameterGroup` resource to specify a MemoryDB parameter group and associate it with a cluster. [AWS::MemoryDB::SubnetGroup](../UserGuide/aws-resource-memorydb-subnetgroup.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-memorydb-subnetgroup.md") Use the `SubnetGroup` resource to specify a MemoryDB subnet group and associate it with a cluster. [AWS::MemoryDB::User](../UserGuide/aws-resource-memorydb-user.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-memorydb-user.md") Use the `User` resource to specify a MemoryDB user and add it to an access control list. [AWS::EMR::Studio](../UserGuide/aws-resource-emr-studio.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-emr-studio.md") Use the `IdpAuthUrl` property to specify the authentication endpoint of your identity provider (IdP) when you use IAM authentication and want to let federated users log in to an Amazon EMR Studio with the Studio URL and credentials from your IdP. In the [AsyncInferenceConfig](../UserGuide/aws-properties-sagemaker-endpointconfig-asyncinferenceconfig.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-sagemaker-endpointconfig-asyncinferenceconfig.md") property type, use the `ClientConfig` to configure the behavior of the client SageMaker uses. Use `OutputConfig` to spcify invocation outputs. In the [AsyncInferenceNotificationConfig](../UserGuide/aws-properties-sagemaker-endpointconfig-asyncinferencenotificationconfig.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-sagemaker-endpointconfig-asyncinferencenotificationconfig.md") property, use the `ErrorTopic` and `SuccessTopic` to define Amazon SNS topics to post a notification if the inference fails or completes successfully, respectively. In the [OutputConfig](../UserGuide/aws-properties-sagemaker-endpointconfig-asyncinferenceoutputconfig.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-sagemaker-endpointconfig-asyncinferenceoutputconfig.md") property type use the `KmsKeyId` to encrypt the asynchronous inference output. Use `NotificationConfig` to specify the notification configuration and `S3OutputPath` to specify the output location in S3. | [New resource](aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_Route53RecoveryControl "aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_Route53RecoveryControl")                                                                        | The following resources were released: AWS::Route53RecoveryControl::Cluster, AWS::Route53RecoveryControl::ControlPanel, AWS::Route53RecoveryControl::RoutingControl, AWS::Route53RecoveryControl::SafetyRule [AWS::Route53RecoveryControl::Cluster](../UserGuide/aws-resource-route53recoverycontrol-cluster.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-route53recoverycontrol-cluster.md") Use the `AWS::Route53RecoveryControl::Cluster` to host routing controls, which are simple on/off switches for routing traffic. [AWS::Route53RecoveryControl::ControlPanel](../UserGuide/aws-resource-route53recoverycontrol-controlpanel.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-route53recoverycontrol-controlpanel.md") Use the `AWS::Route53RecoveryControl::ControlPanel` to define a group of routing controls that can be updated together in a single transaction. [AWS::Route53RecoveryControl::RoutingControl](../UserGuide/aws-resource-route53recoverycontrol-routingcontrol.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-route53recoverycontrol-routingcontrol.md") Use the `AWS::Route53RecoveryControl::RoutingControl` to fail over traffic to an application replica, to recover your application across Availability Zones or Regions. [AWS::Route53RecoveryControl::SafetyRule](../UserGuide/aws-resource-route53recoverycontrol-safetyrule.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-route53recoverycontrol-safetyrule.md") Use the `AWS::Route53RecoveryControl::SafetyRule` to configure safeguards for routing controls, to avoid a scenario like stopping all traffic flow by setting all routing controls to off. | [New resource](aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_Route53RecoveryReadiness "aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_Route53RecoveryReadiness")                                                                    | The following resources were released: AWS::Route53RecoveryReadiness::Cell, AWS::Route53RecoveryReadiness::ReadinessCheck, AWS::Route53RecoveryReadiness::RecoveryGroup, AWS::Route53RecoveryReadiness::ResourceSet [AWS::Route53RecoveryReadiness::Cell](../UserGuide/aws-resource-route53recoveryreadiness-cell.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-route53recoveryreadiness-cell.md") Use the `AWS::Route53RecoveryReadiness::Cell` to define a single cell for an application. [AWS::Route53RecoveryReadiness::ReadinessCheck](../UserGuide/aws-resource-route53recoveryreadiness-readinesscheck.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-route53recoveryreadiness-readinesscheck.md") Use the `AWS::Route53RecoveryReadiness::ReadinessCheck` to check application readiness for failover. Amazon Route 53 Application Recovery Controller uses readiness checks to determine the readiness of the resources in a resource set. [AWS::Route53RecoveryReadiness::RecoveryGroup](../UserGuide/aws-resource-route53recoveryreadiness-recoverygroup.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-route53recoveryreadiness-recoverygroup.md") Use the `AWS::Route53RecoveryReadiness::RecoveryGroup` to define a recovery group for an application. A recovery group models an application and includes cells that represent application replicas. [AWS::Route53RecoveryReadiness::ResourceSet](../UserGuide/aws-resource-route53recoveryreadiness-resourceset.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-route53recoveryreadiness-resourceset.md") Use the `AWS::Route53RecoveryReadiness::ResourceSet` to define a group of resources of a single type that you can associate with a readiness check. | [Updated resource](aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_SSM "aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_SSM")                                                                                                          | The following resource was updated: AWS::SSM::Document [AWS::SSM::Document](../UserGuide/aws-resource-ssm-document.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-ssm-document.md") Use the `Attachments` property to specify a list of key and value pairs that describe attachments to a version of a document. Use the `Requires` property to specify a list of SSM documents required by a document. This parameter is used exclusively by AWS AppConfig. When a user creates an AWS AppConfig configuration in an SSM document, the user must also specify a required document for validation purposes. In this case, an ApplicationConfiguration document requires an ApplicationConfigurationSchema document for validation purposes. For more information, see [Creating a configuration and a configuration profile](../../../appconfig/latest/userguide/appconfig-creating-configuration-and-profile.md "../../../appconfig/latest/userguide/appconfig-creating-configuration-and-profile.md") in the _AWS AppConfig User Guide_. | [New resource](aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_Location "aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_Location")                                                                                                    | The following resources were added: `AWS::Location::GeofenceCollection`, `AWS::Location::Map`, `AWS::Location::PlaceIndex`, `AWS::Location::RouteCalculator`, `AWS::Location::Tracker`, and `AWS::Location::TrackerConsumer`. [AWS::Location::GeofenceCollection](../UserGuide/aws-resource-location-geofencecollection.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-location-geofencecollection.md") Use the `AWS::Location::GeofenceCollection` resource to specify the ability to detect and act when a tracked device enters or exits a defined geographical boundary. [AWS::Location::Map](../UserGuide/aws-resource-location-map.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-location-map.md") Use the `AWS::Location::Map` resource to specify a map resource in your AWS account, which provides map tiles of different styles sourced from available data providers. [AWS::Location::PlaceIndex](../UserGuide/aws-resource-location-placeindex.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-location-placeindex.md") Use the `AWS::Location::PlaceIndex` resource to specify a place index resource in your AWS account, which supports Places functions with geospatial data sourced from your chosen data provider. [AWS::Location::RouteCalculator](../UserGuide/aws-resource-location-routecalculator.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-location-routecalculator.md") Use the `AWS::Location::RouteCalculator` resource to specify a route calculator resource in your AWS account. [AWS::Location::Tracker](../UserGuide/aws-resource-location-tracker.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-location-tracker.md") Use the `AWS::Location::Tracker` resource to specify a tracker resource in your AWS account, which lets you receive current and historical location of devices. [AWS::Location::TrackerConsumer](../UserGuide/aws-resource-location-trackerconsumer.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-location-trackerconsumer.md") Use the `AWS::Location::TrackerConsumer` resource to specify an association between a geofence collection and a tracker resource.
