      | June 7, 2021       |
| [Updated resources](aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_MediaPackage "aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_MediaPackage")                                                                                       | The following resources were updated: AWS::MediaPackage::Channel, AWS::MediaPackage::OriginEndpoint, AWS::MediaPackage::PackagingConfiguration, and AWS::MediaPackage::PackagingGroup. [AWS::MediaPackage::Channel.](../UserGuide/aws-resource-mediapackage-channel.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-mediapackage-channel.md") Use the `EgressAccessLogs` property to specify egress access logs for your channel. Use the `IngressAccessLogs` property to specify ingress access logs for your channel. [AWS::MediaPackage::OriginEndpoint.](../UserGuide/aws-resource-mediapackage-originendpoint.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-mediapackage-originendpoint.md") Use the `CmafEncryption.ConstantInitializationVector` property to specify an optional 128-bit, 16-byte hex value represented by a 32-character string, used in conjunction with the key for encrypting blocks. If you don't specify a value, then AWS Elemental MediaPackage creates the constant initialization vector (IV). [AWS::MediaPackage::PackagingConfiguration.](../UserGuide/aws-resource-mediapackage-packagingconfiguration.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-mediapackage-packagingconfiguration.md") Use the `CmafPackage.IncludeEncoderConfigurationInSegments` property to place your encoder's metadata into every video segment instead of the init fragment, which is the default behavior. This lets you use different SPS/PPS/VPS settings for your assets during content playback. [AWS::MediaPackage::PackagingGroup.](../UserGuide/aws-resource-mediapackage-packaginggroup.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-mediapackage-packaginggroup.md") Use the `EgressAccessLogs` property to configure egress access logs for your packaging group. | [Updated resources](aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_WAFv2 "aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_WAFv2")                                                                                                     | The following resources were updated: AWS::WAFv2::WebACL and AWS::WAFv2::RuleGroup. [AWS::WAFv2::WebACL](../UserGuide/aws-resource-wafv2-webacl.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-wafv2-webacl.md") You can now nest rule statements without using different names for statements at different levels. For example, instead of using `AndStatementOne` and `AndStatementTwo` to nest an `AND` rule statement inside another `AND` rule statement, you can use `AndStatement` for both. The new statement properties are `AndStatement`, `NotStatement`, `OrStatement`, `RateBasedStatement`, and `Statement`. [AWS::WAFv2::RuleGroup](../UserGuide/aws-resource-wafv2-rulegroup.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-wafv2-rulegroup.md") You can now nest rule statements without using different names for statements at different levels. For example, instead of using `AndStatementOne` and `AndStatementTwo` to nest an `AND` rule statement inside another `AND` rule statement, you can use `AndStatement` for both. The new statement properties are `AndStatement`, `NotStatement`, `OrStatement`, `RateBasedStatement`, and `Statement`. | [Updated resources](aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_DataBrew "aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_DataBrew")                                                                                               | The following resources were updated: AWS::DataBrew::Dataset and AWS::DataBrew::Job [AWS::DataBrew::Dataset](../UserGuide/aws-resource-databrew-dataset.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-databrew-dataset.md") Use the `CsvOptions` property to define how DataBrew will read a comma-separated value (CSV) file when creating a dataset from that file. Use the `DatabaseInputDefinition` property to define connection information for dataset input files stored in a database. Use the `DataCatalogInputDefinition` property to define how metadata stored in the AWS Glue Data Catalog is defined in a DataBrew dataset. Use the `DatasetParameter` property to define the type and conditions for a parameter in the Amazon S3 path of the dataset. Use the `DatetimeOptions` property to define the correct interpretation of datetime parameters used in the Amazon S3 path of a dataset. Use the `ExcelOptions` property to define how DataBrew will interpret a Microsoft Excel file when creating a dataset from that file. Use the `FilesLimit` property to limit the number of Amazon S3 files that should be selected for a dataset from a connected Amazon S3 path. Use the `FilterExpression` property to define parameter conditions. Use the `FilterValue` property to define a single entry in the `ValuesMap` of a `FilterExpression`. Use the `FormatOptions` property to define the structure of either comma-separated value (CSV), Excel, or JSON input. Use the `Input` property to define how DataBrew can find data, in either the AWS Glue Data Catalog or Amazon S3. Use the `JsonOptions` property to define how input is to be interpreted by AWS Glue DataBrew. Use the `PathOptions` property to define how DataBrew selects files for a given Amazon S3 path in a dataset. Use the `PathParameter` property to define the file format of a dataset. Use the `S3Location` property to define a single entry in the path parameters of a dataset. [AWS::DataBrew::Job](../UserGuide/aws-resource-databrew-job.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-databrew-job.md") Use the `JobSample` property to define the number of rows on which a profile job is run. Use the `OutputLocation` property to define the location in Amazon S3 where the job writes its output. Use the `Recipe` property to define the actions to be performed on a dataset. | [Updated resources](aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_WAFv2 "aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_WAFv2")                                                                                                     | The following resources were updated: AWS::WAFv2::WebACL and AWS::WAFv2::RuleGroup. [AWS::WAFv2::WebACL](../UserGuide/aws-resource-wafv2-webacl.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-wafv2-webacl.md") You can now inspect a web request body as JSON. You can now add custom request and response handling to web ACL default action and rule action settings. You can now define labels for rules, which are added automatically to matching requests and that persist with requests during web ACL evaluation. You can match against labels using the new rule `LabelMatchStatement`. You can now add a scope-down statement to managed rule group statements. [AWS::WAFv2::RuleGroup](../UserGuide/aws-resource-wafv2-rulegroup.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-wafv2-rulegroup.md") You can now inspect a web request body as JSON. You can now add custom request and response handling to rule action settings. You can now define labels for rules, which are added automatically to matching requests and that persist with requests during web ACL evaluation. You can match against labels using the new rule `LabelMatchStatement`. | [Updated resources](aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_AppMesh "aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_AppMesh")                                                                                                 | The following resources were updated: AWS::AppMesh::VirtualNode and AWS::AppMesh::VirtualGateway [AWS::AppMesh::VirtualNode](../UserGuide/aws-resource-appmesh-virtualnode.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-appmesh-virtualnode.md") Use the `ClientTlsCertificate` property to represent the client's certificate. Use the `SubjectAlternativeNames` property to represent the subject alternative names secured by the certificate. Use the `TlsValidationContextSdsTrust` property to represent a Transport Layer Security (TLS) Secret Discovery Service validation context trust. Use the `ListenerTlsValidationContextTrust` property to represent a listener's Transport Layer Security (TLS) validation context trust. Use the `SubjectAlternativeNameMatchers` property to represent the methods by which a subject alternative name on a peer Transport Layer Security (TLS) certificate can be matched. Use the `ListenerTlsSdsCertificate` property to represent the listener's Secret Discovery Service certificate. Use the `ListenerTlsValidationContext` property to represent a listener's Transport Layer Security (TLS) validation context. [AWS::AppMesh::VirtualGateway](../UserGuide/aws-resource-appmesh-virtualgateway.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-appmesh-virtualgateway.md") Use the `VirtualGatewayListenerTlsValidationContextTrust` property to specify validation context trust. Use the `VirtualGatewayTlsValidationContextSdsTrust` property to represent a virtual gateway's listener's Transport Layer Security (TLS) Secret Discovery Service validation context trust. Use the `SubjectAlternativeNames` property represents the subject alternative names secured by the certificate. Use the `VirtualGatewayListenerTlsSdsCertificate` property to represent the virtual gateway's listener's Secret Discovery Service certificate. Use the `VirtualGatewayClientTlsCertificate` property to represent the virtual gateway's client's Transport Layer Security (TLS) certificate. Use the `VirtualGatewayListenerTlsValidationContext` property to represent a virtual gateway's listener's Transport Layer Security (TLS) validation context. Use the `SubjectAlternativeNameMatchers` property to represent the methods by which a subject alternative name on a peer Transport Layer Security (TLS) certificate can be matched. [AWS::EC2::TransitGatewayMulticastDomain](../UserGuide/aws-resource-ec2-transitgatewaymulticastdomain.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-ec2-transitgatewaymulticastdomain.md") Use the `TransitGatewayMulticastDomain` resource to create a transit gateway multicast domain. [AWS::EC2::TransitGatewayMulticastDomainAssociation](../UserGuide/aws-resource-ec2-transitgatewaymulticastdomainassociation.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-ec2-transitgatewaymulticastdomainassociation.md") Use the `TransitGatewayMulticastDomainAssociation` resource to associate the specified subnets and transit gateway attachments with the specified transit gateway multicast domain. [AWS::EC2::TransitGatewayMulticastGroupMember](../UserGuide/aws-resource-ec2-transitgatewaymulticastgroupmember.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-ec2-transitgatewaymulticastgroupmember.md") Use the `TransitGatewayMulticastGroupMembers` resource to register members (network interfaces) with the transit gateway multicast group. [AWS::EC2::TransitGatewayMulticastGroupSource](../UserGuide/aws-resource-ec2-transitgatewaymulticastgroupsource.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-ec2-transitgatewaymulticastgroupsource.md") Use the `TransitGatewayMulticastGroupSource` resource to register sources (network interfaces) with the specified transit gateway multicast group. [AWS::IoTWireless::Destination](../UserGuide/aws-resource-iotwireless-destination.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-iotwireless-destination.md") Use the `ExpressionType` property of the resource to specify whether to use a new value `MqttTopic` or to use `RuleName`. [AWS::IoTWireless::DeviceProfile](../UserGuide/aws-resource-iotwireless-deviceprofile.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-iotwireless-deviceprofile.md") Use the new `LoRaWAN` property which is a renaming of the `LoRaWANDeviceProfile` property. [AWS::IoTWireless::ServiceProfile](../UserGuide/aws-resource-iotwireless-serviceprofile.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-iotwireless-serviceprofile.md") Use the new `LoRaWAN` property which is a renaming of the `LoRaWANServiceProfile` property. The property type has not changed from `LoRaWANServiceProfile`. In addition, the property descriptions now list any maximum values, minimum values, and patterns. [AWS::IoTWireless::WirelessDevice](../UserGuide/aws-resource-iotwireless-wirelessdevice.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-iotwireless-wirelessdevice.md") Use the new `LoRaWAN` property which is a renaming of the `LoRaWANDevice` property. The property type has not changed from `LoRaWANDevice`. In addition, the property descriptions now list any maximum values, minimum values, and patterns. [AWS::IoTWireless::WirelessGateway](../UserGuide/aws-resource-iotwireless-wirelessgateway.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-iotwireless-wirelessgateway.md") Use the new `LoRaWAN` property which is a renaming of the `LoRaWANGateway` property. The property type has not changed from `LoRaWANGateway`. In addition, the property descriptions now list any maximum values, minimum values, and patterns. | [Updated resource](aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_SageMaker "aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_SageMaker")                                                                                              | The following resources were updated: AWS::SageMaker::Device, AWS::SageMaker::DeviceFleet, and AWS::SageMaker::Model. [AWS::SageMaker::Device](../UserGuide/aws-resource-sagemaker-device.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-sagemaker-device.md") Use the `DeviceFleetName` property to get the name of the fleet the device belongs to. Use the `Device` property to make the edge device you want to create. Use the `Tags` property to get the tags registered to a specific device. Use the `Device.Device` property/resource to get information about a particular device. Use the `Device.Device.Description` property/resource to get a description of the device. Use the `Device.Device.DeviceName` property/resource to get the device name. Use the `Device.Device.IotThingName` property/resource to get the IoT object name. [AWS::SageMaker::DeviceFleet](../UserGuide/aws-resource-sagemaker-devicefleet.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-sagemaker-devicefleet.md") Use the `DeviceFleet.Description` property to get information about a fleet. Use the `OutputConfig` property to get the output configuration for the fleet. Use the `RoleArn` property to get the ARN of the IoT thing. Use the `Tags` property to get the tags registered to a specific fleet. Use the `EdgeOutputConfig.KmsKeyId` property/resource to set the KMS key ID. Use the `EdgeOutputConfig.S3OutputLocation` property/resource to set the S3 bucket URI. [AWS::SageMaker::Model](../UserGuide/aws-resource-sagemaker-model.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-sagemaker-model.md") Use the `MultiModelConfiguration` property to specify configuration details for a multi-model endpoint. | [New resources](aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_MediaConnect "aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_MediaConnect")                                                                                           | The following resources were added: `AWS::MediaConnect::Flow`, `AWS::MediaConnect::FlowEntitlement`, `AWS::MediaConnect::FlowOutput`, `AWS::MediaConnect::FlowSource`, and `AWS::MediaConnect::FlowVpcInterface`. [AWS::MediaConnect::Flow](../UserGuide/aws-resource-mediaconnect-flow.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-mediaconnect-flow.md") Use the `AWS::MediaConnect::Flow` resource to create a connection between one or more video sources and one or more outputs. [AWS::MediaConnect::FlowEntitlement](../UserGuide/aws-resource-mediaconnect-flowentitlement.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-mediaconnect-flowentitlement.md") Use the `AWS::MediaConnect::FlowEntitlement` resource to grant permission to another AWS account to allow access to the content in a specific AWS Elemental MediaConnect flow. [AWS::MediaConnect::FlowOutput](../UserGuide/aws-resource-mediaconnect-flowoutput.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-mediaconnect-flowoutput.md") Use the `AWS::MediaConnect::FlowOutput` resource to define the destination address, protocol, and port that you want MediaConnect to send the ingested video to. [AWS::MediaConnect::FlowSource](../UserGuide/aws-resource-mediaconnect-flowsource.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-mediaconnect-flowsource.md") Use the `AWS::MediaConnect::FlowSource` resource to define where the external video content comes from. [AWS::MediaConnect::FlowVpcInterface](../UserGuide/aws-resource-mediaconnect-flowvpcinterface.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-mediaconnect-flowvpcinterface.md") Use the `AWS::MediaConnect::FlowVpcInterface` resource to create a connection between your MediaConnect flow and a virtual private cloud (VPC) that you created using the Amazon Virtual Private Cloud service. | [New Resources](aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_DataSync "aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_DataSync")                                                                                                   | The following resources were added: AWS::DataSync::Agent, AWS::DataSync::LocationEFS, AWS::DataSync::LocationFSxWindows, AWS::DataSync::LocationNFS, AWS::DataSync::LocationObjectStorage, AWS::DataSync::LocationS3, AWS::DataSync::LocationSMB, and AWS::DataSync::Task. [AWS::DataSync::Agent](../UserGuide/aws-resource-datasync-agent.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-datasync-agent.md") Use the `AWS::DataSync::Agent` resource to specify an AWS DataSync agent. [AWS::DataSync::LocationEFS](../UserGuide/aws-resource-datasync-locationefs.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-datasync-locationefs.md") Use the `AWS::DataSync::LocationEFS` resource to specify a location for an Amazon EFS location. [AWS::DataSync::LocationFSxWindows](../UserGuide/aws-resource-datasync-locationfsxwindows.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-datasync-locationfsxwindows.md") Use the `AWS::DataSync::LocationFSxWindows` resource to specify an Amazon FSx for Windows Server file system. [AWS::DataSync::LocationNFS](../UserGuide/aws-resource-datasync-locationnfs.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-datasync-locationnfs.md") Use the `AWS::DataSync::LocationNFS` resource to specify a file system on a Network File System (NFS) server. [AWS::DataSync::LocationObjectStorage](../UserGuide/aws-resource-datasync-locationobjectstorage.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-datasync-locationobjectstorage.md") Use the `AWS::DataSync::LocationObjectStorage` resource to specify an endpoint for a self-managed object storage bucket. [AWS::DataSync::LocationS3](../UserGuide/aws-resource-datasync-locations3.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-datasync-locations3.md") Use the `AWS::DataSync::LocationS3` resource to specify an endpoint for an Amazon S3 bucket. [AWS::DataSync::LocationSMB](../UserGuide/aws-resource-datasync-locationsmb.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-datasync-locationsmb.md") Use the `AWS::DataSync::LocationSMB` resource to specify a Server Message Block (SMB) location. [AWS::DataSync::Task](../UserGuide/aws-resource-datasync-task.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-datasync-task.md") Use the `AWS::DataSync::Task` resource to specify a task. | [New resources](aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_DevOpsGuru "aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_DevOpsGuru")                                                                                               | The following resources were added: `AWS::DevOpsGuru::NotificationChannel`, `AWS::DevOpsGuru::ResourceCollection` [AWS::DevOpsGuru::NotificationChannel](../UserGuide/aws-resource-devopsguru-notificationchannel.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-devopsguru-notificationchannel.md") Use the `AWS::DevOpsGuru::NotificationChannel` resource to add a notification channel to Amazon DevOps Guru. The notification channel is used to notify you about important events. For example, the creation of an insight or a change in an insight's severity. [AWS::DevOpsGuru::ResourceCollection](../UserGuide/aws-resource-devopsguru-resourcecollection.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-devopsguru-resourcecollection.md") Use the `AWS::DevOpsGuru::ResourceCollection` resource to specify a collection of resources in your account that you want Amazon DevOps Guru to analyze. The specified resources are analyzed to generate insights that contain recommendations, related metrics, and operational data to help you improve the performance of your operational solutions. | [New resources](aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_SageMaker "aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_SageMaker")                                                                                                 | The following resources were added: AWS::SageMaker::DataQualityJobDefinition, AWS::SageMaker::Device, AWS::SageMaker::DeviceFleet, AWS::SageMaker::ModelBiasJobDefinition, AWS::SageMaker::ModelExplainabilityJobDefinition, AWS::SageMaker::ModelQualityJobDefinition, AWS::SageMaker::ModelPackageGroup, and AWS::SageMaker::Pipeline. [AWS::SageMaker::DataQualityJobDefinition](../UserGuide/aws-resource-sagemaker-dataqualityjobdefinition.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-sagemaker-dataqualityjobdefinition.md") Use the `AWS::SageMaker::DataQualityJobDefinition` resource to create a monitoring job that monitors drift in data quality. [AWS::SageMaker::Device](../UserGuide/aws-resource-sagemaker-device.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-sagemaker-device.md") Use the `AWS::SageMaker::Device` resource to register your Devices against an existing SageMaker Edge Manager DeviceFleet. Each device must be listed individually in the CFN specification. [AWS::SageMaker::DeviceFleet](../UserGuide/aws-resource-sagemaker-devicefleet.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-sagemaker-devicefleet.md") Use the `AWS::SageMaker::DeviceFleet` resource to create a DeviceFleet that manages your SageMaker Edge Manager Devices. You must register your devices against the `DeviceFleet` separately. [AWS::SageMaker::ModelBiasJobDefinition](../UserGuide/aws-resource-sagemaker-modelbiasjobdefinition.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-sagemaker-modelbiasjobdefinition.md") Use the `AWS::SageMaker::ModelBiasJobDefinition` resource to create a monitoring job that monitors potential bias in your model. [AWS::SageMaker::ModelExplainabilityJobDefinition](../UserGuide/aws-resource-sagemaker-modelexplainabilityjobdefinition.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-sagemaker-modelexplainabilityjobdefinition.md") Use the `AWS::SageMaker::ModelExplainabilityJobDefinition` resource to create a monitoring job that monitors feature attribution drift in your model. [AWS::SageMaker::ModelQualityJobDefinition](../UserGuide/aws-resource-sagemaker-modelqualityjobdefinition.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-sagemaker-modelqualityjobdefinition.md") Use the `AWS::SageMaker::ModelQualityJobDefinition` resource to create a monitoring job that monitors quality drift in your model. [AWS::SageMaker::ModelPackageGroup](../UserGuide/aws-resource-sagemaker-modelpackagegroup.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-sagemaker-modelpackagegroup.md") Use the `AWS::SageMaker::ModelPackageGroup` resource to create a group of related models. [AWS::SageMaker::Pipeline](../UserGuide/aws-resource-sagemaker-pipeline.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-sagemaker-pipeline.md") Use the `AWS::SageMaker::Pipeline` resource to specify shell scripts that run when you create and/or start a SageMaker Pipeline. For information about SageMaker Pipelines, see [SageMaker Pipelines](../../../sagemaker/latest/dg/pipelines.md "../../../sagemaker/latest/dg/pipelines.md") in the _Amazon SageMaker Developer Guide_. | [Updated resource](aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_Batch "aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_Batch")                                                                                                      | The following resource was updated: [AWS::Batch::JobDefinition](../UserGuide/aws-resource-batch-jobdefinition.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-batch-jobdefinition.md").These property types were added. [LogConfiguration](../UserGuide/aws-properties-batch-jobdefinition-containerproperties-logconfiguration.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-batch-jobdefinition-containerproperties-logconfiguration.md") Use the [LogConfiguration](../UserGuide/aws-properties-batch-jobdefinition-containerproperties-logconfiguration.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-batch-jobdefinition-containerproperties-logconfiguration.md") property type to specify the log configuration options to send to a custom log driver for the container. [Secrets](../UserGuide/aws-properties-batch-jobdefinition-secret.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-batch-jobdefinition-secret.md") Use the [Secrets](../UserGuide/aws-properties-batch-jobdefinition-secret.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-batch-jobdefinition-secret.md") property type to specify a secret to expose to the container. [Tmpfs](../UserGuide/aws-properties-batch-jobdefinition-tmpfs.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-batch-jobdefinition-tmpfs.md") Use the [Tmpfs](../UserGuide/aws-properties-batch-jobdefinition-tmpfs.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-batch-jobdefinition-tmpfs.md") property type to specify the details of a `tmpfs` mount. These property types were updated. [ContainerProperties](../UserGuide/aws-properties-batch-jobdefinition-containerproperties.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-batch-jobdefinition-containerproperties.md") These properties were added. ExecutionRoleArn Specifies the execution role to be assumed for the job. LogConfiguration Specifies the log configuration for a custom log driver for the job. Secrets Specifies the secrets provided for the job. [LinuxParameters](../UserGuide/aws-properties-batch-jobdefinition-containerproperties-linuxparameters.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-batch-jobdefinition-containerproperties-linuxparameters.md") These properties were added. InitProcessEnabled Indicates that an init process should be enabled inside the container that forwards signals and reaps processes. MaxSwap Specifies the total amount of swap memory (in MiB) a job can use. SharedMemorySize Specifies the size (in MiB) of the `/dev/shm` volume. Swappiness Specifies the job container's memory swappiness behavior. Tmpfs Specifies the details of the job's `tmpfs` mount. In the [AWS::CloudFront::CachePolicy ParametersInCacheKeyAndForwardedToOrigin](../UserGuide/aws-properties-cloudfront-cachepolicy-parametersincachekeyandforwardedtoorigin.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-cloudfront-cachepolicy-parametersincachekeyandforwardedtoorigin.md") property type, use the `EnableAcceptEncodingBrotli` property to enable CloudFront to serve compressed objects to viewers that support the Brotli compression format. [AWS::WAFv2::WebACL](../UserGuide/aws-resource-wafv2-webacl.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-wafv2-webacl.md") Rule statements that use IP addresses now support using IP addresses that are forwarded in an HTTP header in the web request, instead of using the IP address that's reported by the web request origin. This option is available for all rule statements that use an IP address: `GeoMatchStatement`, `RateBasedStatement`, and `IPSetReferenceStatement`. The following new properties support this functionality: `IPSetForwardedIPConfiguration` and `ForwardedIPConfiguration`. [AWS::WAFv2::RuleGroup](../UserGuide/aws-resource-wafv2-rulegroup.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-wafv2-rulegroup.md") Rule statements that use IP addresses now support using IP addresses that are forwarded in an HTTP header in the web request, instead of using the IP address that's reported by the web request origin. This option is available for all rule statements that use an IP address: `GeoMatchStatement`, `RateBasedStatement`, and `IPSetReferenceStatement`. The following new properties support this functionality: `IPSetForwardedIPConfiguration` and `ForwardedIPConfiguration`. | [Updated resource](aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_SSM "aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_SSM")                                                                                                          | The following resource was updated: `AWS::SSM::Parameter` [AWS::SSM::Parameter](../UserGuide/aws-resource-ssm-parameter.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-ssm-parameter.md") When you create a `String` parameter, you can now specify a DataType value as `aws:ec2:image` to ensure that the parameter value you enter is a valid Amazon Machine Image (AMI) ID format. Support for AMI ID formats lets you avoid updating all your scripts and templates with a new ID each time the AMI that you want to use in your processes changes. You can create a parameter with the data type `aws:ec2:image`, and for its value, enter the ID of an AMI. This is the AMI from which you currently want new instances to be created. You then reference this parameter in your templates and commands. When you’re ready to use a different AMI, update the parameter value. Parameter Store validates the new AMI ID, and you don’t need to update your scripts and templates. | [New resources](aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_NetworkManager "aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_NetworkManager")                                                                                       | The following resources were added: AWS::NetworkManager::CustomerGatewayAssociation, AWS::NetworkManager::Device, AWS::NetworkManager::GlobalNetwork, AWS::NetworkManager::Link, AWS::NetworkManager::LinkAssociation, AWS::NetworkManager::Site, and AWS::NetworkManager::TransitGatewayRegistration [AWS::NetworkManager::CustomerGatewayAssociation](../UserGuide/aws-resource-networkmanager-customergatewayassociation.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-networkmanager-customergatewayassociation.md") Use the `AWS::NetworkManager::CustomerGatewayAssociation` resource to specify an association between a customer gateway, device, and link. [AWS::NetworkManager::Device](../UserGuide/aws-resource-networkmanager-device.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-networkmanager-device.md") Use the `AWS::NetworkManager::Device` resource to specify a device in a global network. [AWS::NetworkManager::GlobalNetwork](../UserGuide/aws-resource-networkmanager-globalnetwork.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-networkmanager-globalnetwork.md") Use the `AWS::NetworkManager::GlobalNetwork` resource to specify a global network. [AWS::NetworkManager::Link](../UserGuide/aws-resource-networkmanager-link.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-networkmanager-link.md") Use the `AWS::NetworkManager::Link` resource to specify a link for a site. [AWS::NetworkManager::LinkAssociation](../UserGuide/aws-resource-networkmanager-linkassociation.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-networkmanager-linkassociation.md") Use the `AWS::NetworkManager::LinkAssociation` resource to specify an association between a device and a link. [AWS::NetworkManager::Site](../UserGuide/aws-resource-networkmanager-site.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-networkmanager-site.md") Use the `AWS::NetworkManager::Site` resource to specify a site in a global network. [AWS::NetworkManager::TransitGatewayRegistration](../UserGuide/aws-resource-networkmanager-transitgatewayregistration.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-networkmanager-transitgatewayregistration.md") Use the `AWS::NetworkManager::TransitGatewayRegistration` resource to specify the registration of a transit gateway in a global network. [AWS WAFv2](../UserGuide/AWS_WAFv2.md "../UserGuide/AWS_WAFv2.md") Use the web ACL association to define an association between a web ACL and a regional application resource, to protect the resource. A regional application can be an Application Load Balancer (ALB), Amazon API Gateway REST API, an AWS AppSync GraphQL API, or an Amazon Cognito user pool. For Amazon CloudFront distributions, you use `AWS::CloudFront::Distribution` to manage the association. [AWS::ACMPCA::Certificate](../UserGuide/aws-resource-acmpca-certificate.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-acmpca-certificate.md") The `AWS::ACMPCA::Certificate` resource is used to issue a certificate using your private certificate authority. [AWS::ACMPCA::CertificateAuthority](../UserGuide/aws-resource-acmpca-certificateauthority.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-acmpca-certificateauthority.md") Use the `AWS::ACMPCA::CertificateAuthority` resource to create a private CA. [AWS::ACMPCA::CertificateAuthorityActivation](../UserGuide/aws-resource-acmpca-certificateauthorityactivation.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-acmpca-certificateauthorityactivation.md") The `AWS::ACMPCA::CertificateAuthorityActivation` resource creates and installs a CA certificate on a CA. | [New resource](aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_AppConfig "aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_AppConfig")                                                                                                  | The following resources were added: AWS::AppConfig::Application, AWS::AppConfig::ConfigurationProfile, AWS::AppConfig::Deployment, AWS::AppConfig::Environment, and AWS::AppConfig::DeploymentStrategy [AWS::AppConfig::Application](../UserGuide/aws-resource-appconfig-application.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-appconfig-application.md") The `AWS::AppConfig::Application` resource creates an application, which is a logical unit of code that provides capabilities for your customers. [AWS::AppConfig::ConfigurationProfile](../UserGuide/aws-resource-appconfig-configurationprofile.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-appconfig-configurationprofile.md") The `AWS::AppConfig::ConfigurationProfile` resource creates a configuration profile that enables AWS AppConfig to access the configuration source. [AWS::AppConfig::Deployment](../UserGuide/aws-resource-appconfig-deployment.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-appconfig-deployment.md") The `AWS::AppConfig::Deployment` resource starts a deployment. [AWS::AppConfig::Environment](../UserGuide/aws-resource-appconfig-environment.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-appconfig-environment.md") The `AWS::AppConfig::Environment` resource creates an environment, which is a logical deployment group of AWS AppConfig targets, such as applications in a `Beta` or `Production` environment. [AWS::AppConfig::DeploymentStrategy](../UserGuide/aws-resource-appconfig-deploymentstrategy.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-appconfig-deploymentstrategy.md") The `AWS::AppConfig::DeploymentStrategy` resource creates an AWS AppConfig deployment strategy. | [Updated resource](aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_Glue "aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_Glue")                                                                                                        | The following resource was updated: AWS::Glue::Crawler [AWS::Glue::Crawler](../UserGuide/aws-resource-glue-table.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-glue-table.md") Use the `MongoDBTarget` property to specify an Amazon DocumentDB or MongoDB data store to crawl. Use the `RecrawlPolicy.RecrawlBehavior` property to specify a new `CRAWL_EVENT_MODE` that specifies crawling only the changes identified by Amazon S3 events. Use the `S3Target.SampleSize` property to specify the number of files in each leaf folder to be crawled when crawling sample files in a dataset. Use the `S3Target.EventQueueArn` property to specify a valid Amazon SQS ARN. Use the `S3Target.DlqEventQueueArn` property to specify a valid Amazon dead-letter SQS ARN. You can also use tools that are compatible with Prometheus-formatted metrics or tools that integrate with Amazon MSK Open Monitoring. [AWS::SSM::Document](aws-resource-ssm-document.md "aws-resource-ssm-document.md") Use the `Name` property to specify a name for the Systems Manager document. [AWS::RDS::DBInstance](aws-resource-rds-dbinstance.md "aws-resource-rds-dbinstance.md") Use the `MaxAllocatedStorage` property to specify the upper limit to which Amazon RDS can automatically scale the storage of the DB instance. [AWS::Lambda::EventSourceMapping](../UserGuide/aws-resource-lambda-eventsourcemapping.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-lambda-eventsourcemapping.md") For stream sources (DynamoDB and Kinesis), use the `BisectBatchOnFunctionError` property to split the batch in two and retry if the function returns an error. For stream sources (DynamoDB and Kinesis), use the `DestinationConfig` property to specify an Amazon SQS queue or Amazon SNS topic destination for discarded records. For stream sources (DynamoDB and Kinesis), use the `MaximumRecordAgeInSeconds` property to specify the maximum age of a record that Lambda sends to a function for processing. For stream sources (DynamoDB and Kinesis), use the `MaximumRetryAttempts` property to specify the maximum number of times to retry when the function returns an error. For stream sources (DynamoDB and Kinesis), use the `ParallelizationFactor` property to specify the number of batches to process from each shard concurrently. | [New resources](aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_ECS "aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_ECS")                                                                                                             | The following resources were added: AWS::ECS::PrimaryTaskSet, AWS::ECS::TaskSet. [AWS::ECS::PrimaryTaskSet](../UserGuide/aws-resource-ecs-primarytaskset.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-ecs-primarytaskset.md") Use the `AWS::ECS::PrimaryTaskSet` resource to specify which task set in a service is the primary task set. Any parameters that are updated on the primary task set in a service will transition to the service. This is used when a service uses the `EXTERNAL` deployment controller type. [AWS::ECS::TaskSet](../UserGuide/aws-resource-ecs-taskset.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-ecs-taskset.md") Use the `AWS::ECS::TaskSet` resource to create a task set in the specified cluster and service. This is used when a service uses the `EXTERNAL` deployment controller type. [AWS::CloudWatch::InsightRule](../UserGuide/aws-resource-cloudwatch-insightrule.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-cloudwatch-insightrule.md") Use the `AWS::CloudWatch::InsightRule` property to create a Contributor Insights rule. [AWS WAFv2](../UserGuide/AWS_WAFv2.md "../UserGuide/AWS_WAFv2.md") This is the latest version of AWS WAF, a web application firewall that lets you monitor HTTP(S) requests that are forwarded to an Amazon API Gateway REST API, Amazon CloudFront, Application Load Balancer, an AWS AppSync GraphQL API, or an Amazon Cognito user pool. AWS WAF also lets you control access to your content. [AWS::AppSync::Resolver](../UserGuide/aws-resource-appsync-resolver.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-appsync-resolver.md") Use the `CachingConfig` property to specify the caching behavior of your AWS AppSync resolver. [AWS::AppSync::Resolver](../UserGuide/aws-resource-appsync-resolver.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-appsync-resolver.md") Use the `SyncConfig` property to specify the conflict detection and resolution strategy of your AWS AppSync resolver. [AWS::AppSync::Resolver](../UserGuide/aws-resource-appsync-resolver.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-appsync-resolver.md") Use the `LambdaConflictHandlerConfig` property to specify the ARN of the lambda that is used for handling conflicts in your AWS AppSync resolver. [AWS::AppSync::DataSource](../UserGuide/aws-resource-appsync-datasource.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-appsync-datasource.md") Use the `DeltaSyncConfig` property to specify the delta sync configurations for your versioned AWS AppSync data source. | [Updated resources](aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_ECS "aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_ECS")                                                                                                         | The following resources were updated: AWS::ECS::Cluster, AWS::ECS::Service, and AWS::ECS::TaskDefinition. [AWS::ECS::Cluster](../UserGuide/aws-resource-ecs-cluster.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-ecs-cluster.md") Use the `ClusterSettings` property to specify the setting to use when creating a cluster. This parameter is used to use CloudWatch Container Insights for a cluster. [AWS::ECS::Service](../UserGuide/aws-resource-ecs-service.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-ecs-service.md") Use the `DeploymentController` property to specify the deployment controller to use for the service. [AWS::ECS::TaskDefinition](../UserGuide/aws-resource-ecs-taskdefinition.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-ecs-taskdefinition.md") In the [ContainerDefinition](../UserGuide/aws-properties-ecs-taskdefinition-containerdefinitions.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-ecs-taskdefinition-containerdefinitions.md") property type, use the `FirelensConfiguration` property to specify the FireLens configuration for the container. This is used to specify and configure a log router for container logs. In the [LinuxParameters](../UserGuide/aws-properties-ecs-taskdefinition-linuxparameters.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-ecs-taskdefinition-linuxparameters.md") property type: <br>• use the `MaxSwap` property to specify the total amount of swap memory (in MiB) a container can use. <br>• use the `Swappiness` property to tune a container's memory swappiness behavior. A `swappiness` value of `0` will cause swapping to not happen unless absolutely necessary. A `swappiness` value of `100` will cause pages to be swapped very aggressively. | [Updated resources](aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_RDS "aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_RDS")                                                                                                         | The following resources were updated: AWS::RDS::DBCluster and AWS::RDS::DBInstance. [AWS::RDS::DBCluster](../UserGuide/aws-resource-rds-dbcluster.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-rds-dbcluster.md") Use the `EnableHttpEndpoint` property to indicate whether to enable the HTTP endpoint for an Aurora Serverless DB cluster. By default, the HTTP endpoint is disabled. When enabled, the HTTP endpoint provides a connectionless web service API for running SQL queries on the Aurora Serverless DB cluster. You can also query your database from inside the RDS console with the query editor. [AWS::RDS::DBInstance](../UserGuide/aws-properties-rds-database-instance.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-rds-database-instance.md") For Oracle DB instances, Amazon RDS can use Kerberos Authentication to authenticate users that connect to the DB instance. | [Updated resources](aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_GameLift "aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_GameLift")                                                                                               | The following resources were updated: AWS::GameLift::Build, AWS::GameLift::Fleet. [AWS::GameLift::Build](../UserGuide/aws-resource-gamelift-build.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-gamelift-build.md") Use the `OperatingSystem` property to specify the operating system that the build files run on. [AWS::GameLift::Fleet](../UserGuide/aws-resource-gamelift-fleet.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-gamelift-fleet.md") Use the `CertificateConfiguration` property to generate a TLS/SSL certificate for the new fleet. Use the `FleetType` property to specify use of On-Demand or Spot instances in the fleet. Use the `InstanceRoleArn` property to manage access to your non-GameLift AWS resources from GameLift fleet instances. Use the `MetricGroups` property to add fleet metrics to a CloudWatch metric group. Use the `NewGameSessionProtectionPolicy` property to prevent the fleet's active game sessions from being terminated during a scale down event. Use the `PeerVpcAwsAccountId` property when setting up VPC peering for the fleet. Use the `PeerVpcId` property when setting up VPC peering for the fleet. Use the `ResourceCreationLimitPolicy` property to limit an individual player's ability to use the fleet's available hosting resources. Use the `RuntimeConfiguration` property to configure what processes are run on each instance in the fleet. Use the `ScriptId` property to create a Realtime Servers fleet and configure it with a Realtime script. [AWS::GameLift::Script](../UserGuide/aws-resource-gamelift-script.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-gamelift-script.md") Use the `Script` resource to upload a configuration script for a Realtime Servers fleet. [AWS::GameLift::GameSessionQueue](../UserGuide/aws-resource-gamelift-gamesessionqueue.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-gamelift-gamesessionqueue.md") Use the `GameSessionQueue` resource to create a game session queue that processes player requests for new game sessions. [AWS::GameLift::MatchmakingConfiguration](../UserGuide/aws-resource-gamelift-matchmakingconfiguration.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-gamelift-matchmakingconfiguration.md") Use the `MatchmakingConfiguration` resource to create a matchmaker that processes player requests for new matched game sessions. [AWS::GameLift::MatchmakingRuleSet](../UserGuide/aws-resource-gamelift-matchmakingruleset.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-gamelift-matchmakingruleset.md") Use the `MatchmakingRuleSet` resource to create rules that specify how to form matches and evaluate players for inclusion in a match. | Updated resources                                                                                                                                                                                                  | The following resources were updated: `AWS::ApplicationAutoScaling::ScalableTarget`, `AWS::DynamoDB::Table`, `AWS::EC2::Instance`, `AWS::ECS::TaskDefinition`, `AWS::ElastiCache::ReplicationGroup`, `AWS::Events::Rule`, `AWS::IAM::Role`, and `AWS::Lambda::EventSourceMapping`. [AWS::ApplicationAutoScaling::ScalableTarget](aws-resource-applicationautoscaling-scalabletarget.md "aws-resource-applicationautoscaling-scalabletarget.md") Use the `SuspendedState` property to suspend and resume automatic scaling. Setting the value of an attribute to `true` suspends the specified scaling activities. Setting it to `false` (default) resumes the specified scaling activities. [AWS::DynamoDB::Table](aws-resource-dynamodb-table.md "aws-resource-dynamodb-table.md") In the [SSESpecification](aws-properties-dynamodb-table-ssespecification.md "aws-properties-dynamodb-table-ssespecification.md") property type, use the `SSEType` property to specify server-side encryption type. [AWS::EC2::Instance](aws-resource-ec2-instance.md "aws-resource-ec2-instance.md") Use the `CpuOptions` property to specify the CPU options for the instance. In the [Ebs](aws-properties-ec2-instance-ebs.md "aws-properties-ec2-instance-ebs.md") property type, use the `KmsKeyId` property to specify an identifier (key ID, key alias, ID ARN, or alias ARN) for a customer managed key under which the EBS volume is encrypted. [AWS::ECS::TaskDefinition](aws-resource-ecs-taskdefinition.md "aws-resource-ecs-taskdefinition.md") Use the `IpcMode` property to specify the IPC resource namespace to use for the containers in the task. The valid values are `host`, `task`, or `none`. Use the `PidMode` property to specify the process namespace to use for the containers in the task. The valid values are `host` or `task`. In the [ContainerDefinition](aws-properties-ecs-taskdefinition-containerdefinitions.md "aws-properties-ecs-taskdefinition-containerdefinitions.md") property type: <br>• When the `Interactive` property is set to `true`, this allows you to deploy containerized applications that require `stdin` or a `tty` to be allocated. <br>• When the `PseudoTerminal` proprety is set to `true`, a TTY is allocated. <br>• Use the `SystemControls` property to specify a list of namespaced kernel parameters to set in the container. In the [LogConfiguration](aws-properties-ecs-taskdefinition-containerdefinitions-logconfiguration.md "aws-properties-ecs-taskdefinition-containerdefinitions-logconfiguration.md") property type, use the `SecretOptions` property to specify the secrets to pass to the log configuration. [AWS::ElastiCache::ReplicationGroup](aws-resource-elasticache-replicationgroup.md "aws-resource-elasticache-replicationgroup.md") Use the `KmsKeyId` property to specify the ID of the KMS key used to encrypt the disk on the cluster. [AWS::Events::Rule](aws-resource-events-rule.md "aws-resource-events-rule.md") In the [EcsParameters](aws-properties-events-rule-ecsparameters.md "aws-properties-events-rule-ecsparameters.md") property type: <br>• Use the `Group` property to specify an ECS task group for the task. <br>• Use the `LaunchType` property to specify the launch type on which your task is running. <br>• If the ECS task uses the `awsvpc` network mode, use the `NetworkConfiguration` property to specify the VPC subnets and security groups associated with the task and whether a public IP address is to be used. <br>• Use the `PlatformVersion` property to specify the platform version for the task. [AWS::IAM::Role](aws-resource-iam-role.md "aws-resource-iam-role.md") Use the `Description` property to provide a description for the role. Use the `Tags` property to specify a list of tags that are attached to the specified role. [AWS::Lambda::EventSourceMapping](aws-resource-lambda-eventsourcemapping.md "aws-resource-lambda-eventsourcemapping.md") Use the `MaximumBatchingWindowInSeconds` property to specify the maximum amount of time to gather records before invoking the function, in seconds. | [Updated resources](aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_RDS "aws-template-resource-type-ref.md#AWS_RDS")                                                                                                         | The following resources were updated: AWS::RDS::DBCluster and AWS::RDS::DBInstance [AWS::RDS::DBCluster](../UserGuide/aws-resource-rds-dbcluster.md "../UserGuide/aws-resource-rds-dbcluster.md") Use the `AssociatedRoles` property to specify the AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) roles associated with the DB instance. Use the `RestoreType` property to specify the type of restore to be performed. Use the `SourceDBClusterIdentifier` property to specify the identifier of the source DB cluster from which to restore. Use the `UseLatestRestorableTime` property to specify whether to restore the DB cluster to the latest restorable backup time. [AWS::RDS::DBInstance](../UserGuide/aws-properties-rds-database-instance.md "../UserGuide/aws-properties-rds-database-instance.md") Use the `AssociatedRoles` property to specify the AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) roles associated with the DB instance. | Updated resources                                                                                                                                                                                                  | The following resources were updated: `AWS::Batch::JobDefinition`, `AWS::Cognito::UserPool`, `AWS::Cognito::UserPoolClient`, and `AWS::Glue::Job`. [AWS::Batch::JobDefinition](aws-resource-batch-jobdefinition.md "aws-resource-batch-jobdefinition.md") In the [ContainerProperties](aws-properties-batch-jobdefinition-containerproperties.md "aws-properties-batch-jobdefinition-containerproperties.md") property type, use the `LinuxParameters` property to specify Linux-specific modifications that are applied to the container, such as details for device mappings. [AWS::Cognito::UserPool](aws-resource-cognito-userpool.md "aws-resource-cognito-userpool.md") Use the `UserPoolAddOns` property to enable advanced security risk detection. Use the `VerificationMessageTemplate` property to define the template for verification messages. [AWS::Cognito::UserPoolClient](aws-resource-cognito-userpoolclient.md "aws-resource-cognito-userpoolclient.md") Use the `AnalyticsConfiguration` property to define the Amazon Pinpoint analytics configuration for collecting metrics for this user pool. [AWS::Glue::Job](aws-resource-glue-job.md "aws-resource-glue-job.md") Use the `GlueVersion` property to determine the versions of Apache Spark and Python that AWS Glue supports. The Python version indicates the version supported for jobs of type Spark. Use the `MaxCapacity` property to specify the number of AWS Glue data processing units (DPUs) that can be allocated when this job runs. A DPU is a relative measure of processing power that consists of 4 vCPUs of compute capacity and 16 GB of memory. For the `NumberofWorkers` property, when you specify a Python shell job (`JobCommand.Name`="pythonshell"), you can allocate either 0.0625 or 1 DPU. The default is 0.0625 DPU. When you specify an Apache Spark ETL job (`JobCommand.Name`="glueetl"), you can allocate from 2 to 100 DPUs. The default is 10 DPUs. This job type can't have a fractional DPU allocation. Use the `WorkerType` property to specify the type of predefined worker that is allocated when a job runs. In the [JobCommand](aws-properties-glue-job-jobcommand.md "aws-properties-glue-job-jobcommand.md") property type, use the `PythonVersion` property to specify the Python version being used to execute a Python shell job. [AWS::MediaLive::Channel](aws-resource-medialive-channel.md "aws-resource-medialive-channel.md") The `AWS::MediaLive::Channel` resource creates a channel. A MediaLive channel ingests and transcodes (decodes and encodes) source content from the inputs that are attached to that channel, and packages the new content into outputs. [AWS::MediaLive::Input](aws-resource-medialive-input.md "aws-resource-medialive-input.md") The `AWS::MediaLive::Input` resource creates an input. A MediaLive input holds information that describes how the MediaLive channel is connected to the upstream system that is providing the source content that is to be transcoded. [AWS::MediaLive::InputSecurityGroup](aws-resource-medialive-inputsecuritygroup.md "aws-resource-medialive-inputsecuritygroup.md") The `AWS::MediaLive::InputSecurityGroup` resource creates an input security group. A MediaLive input security group is associated with a MediaLive input. The input security group is an "allow list" of IP addresses that controls whether an external IP address can push content to the associated MediaLive input. | Updated resources                                                                                                                                                                                                  | The following resources were updated: `AWS::AppMesh::VirtualNode`, `AWS::CodeBuild::Project`, `AWS::EC2::Host`, `AWS::EC2::Route`, `AWS::EC2::VPNConnection`, `AWS::ECS::Cluster`, `AWS::ECS::Service`, `AWS::ECS::TaskDefinition`, `AWS::EFS::MountTarget`, `AWS::ElasticLoadBalancingV2::ListenerRule`, `AWS::EMR::Cluster`, `AWS::IoTAnalytics::Dataset`, `AWS::KinesisFirehose::DeliveryStream`, `AWS::S3::Bucket`. [AWS::AppMesh::VirtualNode](aws-resource-appmesh-virtualnode.md "aws-resource-appmesh-virtualnode.md") Use `ServiceDiscovery` to specify whether to use `AWSCloudMap` or `DNS` for service discovery. If using AWS Cloud Map for service discovery, use `AwsCloudMapServiceDiscovery` to specify `ServiceName`, `NamespaceName`, and `Attributes` properties. Use `AwsCloudMapInstanceAttribute` to specify key-value pairs for `AwsCloudMapServiceDiscovery`. [AWS::CodeBuild::Project](aws-resource-codebuild-project.md "aws-resource-codebuild-project.md") Use the `SecondarySourceVersions` property to specify an array of `ProjectSourceVersion` objects. If `secondarySourceVersions` is specified at the build level, then they take over these `secondarySourceVersions` (at the project level). [AWS::DLM::LifecyclePolicy](aws-resource-dlm-lifecyclepolicy.md "aws-resource-dlm-lifecyclepolicy.md") In the [PolicyDetails](aws-properties-dlm-lifecyclepolicy-policydetails.md "aws-properties-dlm-lifecyclepolicy-policydetails.md") property type: <br>• Use the `PolicyType` property to determine the valid target resource types and actions a policy can manage. This field defaults to EBS_SNAPSHOT_MANAGEMENT if not present. <br>• Use the `Parameters` property to specify a set of optional parameters that can be provided by the policy. In the [Schedule](aws-properties-dlm-lifecyclepolicy-schedule.md "aws-properties-dlm-lifecyclepolicy-schedule.md") property type, use the `VariableTags` property to specify a collection of key-value pairs with values determined dynamically when the policy is executed. Keys may be any valid Amazon EC2 tag key. Values must be in one of the two following formats: `$(instance-id)` or `$(timestamp)`. Variable tags are only valid for EBS Snapshot Management Instance policies. [AWS::EC2::Host](aws-resource-ec2-host.md "aws-resource-ec2-host.md") Use the `HostRecovery` property to indicates whether to enable or disable host recovery for the Dedicated Host. [AWS::EC2::Route](aws-resource-ec2-route.md "aws-resource-ec2-route.md") Use the `TransitGatewayId` property to specify the ID of a transit gateway. [AWS::EC2::VPNConnection](aws-resource-ec2-vpn-connection.md "aws-resource-ec2-vpn-connection.md") Use the `TransitGatewayId` property to specify the ID of the transit gateway associated with the VPN connection. Use the `VpnGatewayId` property to specify the ID of the virtual private gateway at the AWS side of the VPN connection. [AWS::ECR::Repository](aws-resource-ecr-repository.md "aws-resource-ecr-repository.md") Use the `Tags` property to specify an array of key-value pairs to apply to this resource. [AWS::ECS::Cluster](aws-resource-ecs-cluster.md "aws-resource-ecs-cluster.md") Use the `Tags` property to apply metadata to clusters to help you categorize and organize them. [AWS::ECS::Service](aws-resource-ecs-service.md "aws-resource-ecs-service.md") Use the `EnableECSManagedTags` property to specify whether to enable Amazon ECS managed tags for the tasks within the service. Use the `PropagateTags` property to specify whether to propagate the tags from the task definition or the service to the tasks in the service. Use the `Tags` property to apply metadata to services to help you categorize and organize them. [AWS::ECS::TaskDefinition](aws-resource-ecs-taskdefinition.md "aws-resource-ecs-taskdefinition.md") In the [ContainerDefinition](aws-properties-ecs-taskdefinition-containerdefinitions.md "aws-properties-ecs-taskdefinition-containerdefinitions.md") property type: <br>• Use the `ResourceRequirements` property to specify the type and amount of a resource to assign to a container. The only supported resource is a GPU. <br>• Use the `Secrets` property to specify the secrets to pass to the container. Use the `Tags` property to apply metadata to task definitions to help you categorize and organize them. [AWS::EFS::FileSystem](aws-resource-efs-filesystem.md "aws-resource-efs-filesystem.md") Use the `LifecyclePolicies` property to specify a list of policies used by EFS lifecycle management to transition files to the Infrequent Access (IA) storage class. [AWS::EFS::MountTarget](aws-resource-efs-mounttarget.md "aws-resource-efs-mounttarget.md") Use the `IpAddress` attribute to return the IPv4 address of the mount target. [AWS::ElasticLoadBalancingV2::ListenerRule](aws-resource-elasticloadbalancingv2-listenerrule.md "aws-resource-elasticloadbalancingv2-listenerrule.md") In the [RuleCondition](aws-properties-elasticloadbalancingv2-listenerrule-conditions.md "aws-properties-elasticloadbalancingv2-listenerrule-conditions.md") property type: <br>• Use the `HostHeaderConfig` property to specify information for a host header condition. <br>• Use the `HttpHeaderConfig` property to specify information for an HTTP header condition. <br>• Use the `HttpRequestMethodConfig` property to specify information for an HTTP method condition. <br>• Use the `PathPatternConfig` property to specify information for a path pattern condition. <br>• Use the `QueryStringConfig` property to specify information for a query string condition. <br>• Use the `SourceIpConfig` property to specify information for a source IP condition. [AWS::EMR::Cluster](aws-resource-emr-cluster.md "aws-resource-emr-cluster.md") In the [JobFlowInstancesConfig](aws-properties-emr-cluster-jobflowinstancesconfig.md "aws-properties-emr-cluster-jobflowinstancesconfig.md") property type, use the `Ec2SubnetIds` property to specify multiple EC2 subnet IDs. [AWS::IoTAnalytics::Dataset](aws-resource-iotanalytics-dataset.md "aws-resource-iotanalytics-dataset.md") When data set contents are created they are delivered to destinations specified in the `ContentDeliveryRules` property. Use the `VersioningConfiguration` property to specify how many versions of data set contents are kept. If not specified or set to null, only the latest version plus the latest succeeded version (if they are different) are kept for the time period specified by the "retentionPeriod" parameter. [AWS::KinesisFirehose::DeliveryStream](aws-properties-kinesisfirehose-deliverystream-extendeds3destinationconfiguration.md "aws-properties-kinesisfirehose-deliverystream-extendeds3destinationconfiguration.md") In the [ExtendedS3DestinationConfiguration](aws-properties-kinesisfirehose-deliverystream-extendeds3destinationconfiguration.md "aws-properties-kinesisfirehose-deliverystream-extendeds3destinationconfiguration.md") property type: <br>• Use the `DataFormatConversionConfiguration` property to specify the serializer, deserializer, and schema for converting data from the JSON format to the Parquet or ORC format before writing it to Amazon S3. <br>• Use the `ErrorOutputPrefix` property to specify a prefix that Amazon Data Firehose evaluates and adds to failed records before writing them to S3. <br>• The `Prefix` property is no longer required. In the [S3DestinationConfiguration](aws-properties-kinesisfirehose-deliverystream-s3destinationconfiguration.md "aws-properties-kinesisfirehose-deliverystream-s3destinationconfiguration.md") property type, use the `ErrorOutputPrefix` property to specify a prefix that Amazon Data Firehose evaluates and adds to failed records before writing them to S3. [AWS::S3::Bucket](aws-resource-s3-bucket.md "aws-resource-s3-bucket.md") Use the `ObjectLockConfiguration` property to specify an object lock configuration for the specified bucket. Use the `ObjectLockEnabled` property to specify whether this bucket has an object lock configuration enabled. | June 13, 2019      |
| New resources                                                                                                                                                                                                      | The following resources were added: `AWS::Amplify::App`, `AWS::Amplify::Branch`, `AWS::Amplify::Domain`, `AWS::EC2::ClientVpnAuthorizationRule`, `AWS::EC2::ClientVpnEndpoint`, `AWS::EC2::ClientVpnRoute`, `AWS::EC2::ClientVpnTargetNetworkAssociation`, `AWS::MSK::Cluster`. [AWS::Amplify::App](aws-resource-amplify-app.md "aws-resource-amplify-app.md") Creates apps in AWS Amplify Console. An app is a collection of branches. [AWS::Amplify::Branch](aws-resource-amplify-branch.md "aws-resource-amplify-branch.md") Creates a new branch within an AWS Amplify Console app. [AWS::Amplify::Domain](aws-resource-amplify-domain.md "aws-resource-amplify-domain.md") Allows you to connect a custom domain to your AWS Amplify Console app. [AWS::EC2::ClientVpnAuthorizationRule](aws-resource-ec2-clientvpnauthorizationrule.md "aws-resource-ec2-clientvpnauthorizationrule.md") Specifies an ingress authorization rule to add to a Client VPN endpoint. Ingress authorization rules act as firewall rules that grant access to networks. [AWS::EC2::ClientVpnEndpoint](aws-resource-ec2-clientvpnendpoint.md "aws-resource-ec2-clientvpnendpoint.md") Specifies a Client VPN endpoint. A Client VPN endpoint is the resource you create and configure to enable and manage Client VPN sessions. It is the destination endpoint at which all Client VPN sessions are terminated. [AWS::EC2::ClientVpnRoute](aws-resource-ec2-clientvpnroute.md "aws-resource-ec2-clientvpnroute.md") Specifies a network route to add to a Client VPN endpoint. Each Client VPN endpoint has a route table that describes the available destination network routes. Each route in the route table specifies the path for traﬃc to speciﬁc resources or networks. [AWS::EC2::ClientVpnTargetNetworkAssociation](aws-resource-ec2-clientvpntargetnetworkassociation.md "aws-resource-ec2-clientvpntargetnetworkassociation.md") Specifies a target network to associate with a Client VPN endpoint. A target network is a subnet in a VPC. You can associate multiple subnets from the same VPC with a Client VPN endpoint. [AWS::MSK::Cluster](aws-resource-msk-cluster.md "aws-resource-msk-cluster.md") Use the `AWS::MSK::Cluster` resource to create an Amazon MSK cluster. [AWS::SageMaker::NotebookInstance](aws-resource-sagemaker-notebookinstance.md "aws-resource-sagemaker-notebookinstance.md") Use the `AcceleratorTypes` property to specify a list of Amazon Elastic Inference (EI) instance types to associate with this notebook instance. Use the `AdditionalCodeRepositories` property to specify an array of up to three Git repositories associated with the notebook instance. | New resources                                                                                                                                                                                                      | The following resources were added: `AWS::IoTThingsGraph::FlowTemplate`, `AWS::Pinpoint::ADMChannel`, `AWS::Pinpoint::APNSChannel`, `AWS::Pinpoint::APNSSandboxChannel`, `AWS::Pinpoint::APNSVoipChannel`, `AWS::Pinpoint::APNSVoipSandboxChannel`, `AWS::Pinpoint::App`, `AWS::Pinpoint::ApplicationSettings`, `AWS::Pinpoint::BaiduChannel`, `AWS::Pinpoint::Campaign`, `AWS::Pinpoint::EmailChannel`, `AWS::Pinpoint::EventStream`, `AWS::Pinpoint::GCMChannel`, `AWS::Pinpoint::SMSChannel`, `AWS::Pinpoint::Segment`, `AWS::Pinpoint::VoiceChannel`, `AWS::SageMaker::CodeRepository`, and `AWS::MSK::Cluster`. [AWS::IoTThingsGraph::FlowTemplate](aws-resource-iotthingsgraph-flowtemplate.md "aws-resource-iotthingsgraph-flowtemplate.md") Use the `AWS::IoTThingsGraph::FlowTemplate` resource to specify a workflow template. [AWS::Pinpoint::ADMChannel](aws-resource-pinpoint-admchannel.md "aws-resource-pinpoint-admchannel.md") Use the `AWS::Pinpoint::ADMChannel` resource to specify an ADM channel. You can use the ADM channel to send push notifications through the Amazon Device Messaging (ADM) service to apps that run on Amazon devices, such as Kindle Fire tablets. [AWS::Pinpoint::APNSChannel](aws-resource-pinpoint-apnschannel.md "aws-resource-pinpoint-apnschannel.md") Use the `AWS::Pinpoint::APNSChannel` resource to specify an APNs channel. You can use the APNs channel to send push notification messages to the Apple Push Notification service (APNs). [AWS::Pinpoint::APNSSandboxChannel](aws-resource-pinpoint-apnssandboxchannel.md "aws-resource-pinpoint-apnssandboxchannel.md") Use the `AWS::Pinpoint::APNSSandboxChannel` resource to specify an APNs sandbox channel. You can use the APNs sandbox channel to send push notification messages to the sandbox environment of the Apple Push Notification service (APNs). [AWS::Pinpoint::APNSVoipChannel](aws-resource-pinpoint-apnsvoipchannel.md "aws-resource-pinpoint-apnsvoipchannel.md") Use the `AWS::Pinpoint::APNSVoipChannel` resource to specify an APNs VoIP channel. You can use the APNs VoIP channel to send VoIP notification messages to the Apple Push Notification service (APNs). [AWS::Pinpoint::APNSVoipSandboxChannel](aws-resource-pinpoint-apnsvoipsandboxchannel.md "aws-resource-pinpoint-apnsvoipsandboxchannel.md") Use the `AWS::Pinpoint::APNSVoipSandboxChannel` resource to specify an APNs VoIP sandbox channel. You can use the APNs VoIP sandbox channel to send VoIP notification messages to the sandbox environment of the Apple Push Notification service (APNs). [AWS::Pinpoint::App](aws-resource-pinpoint-app.md "aws-resource-pinpoint-app.md") Use the `AWS::Pinpoint::App` resource to specify an app. [AWS::Pinpoint::ApplicationSettings](aws-resource-pinpoint-applicationsettings.md "aws-resource-pinpoint-applicationsettings.md") Use the `AWS::Pinpoint::ApplicationSettings` resource to specify the settings for an Amazon Pinpoint app. [AWS::Pinpoint::BaiduChannel](aws-resource-pinpoint-baiduchannel.md "aws-resource-pinpoint-baiduchannel.md") Use the `AWS::Pinpoint::BaiduChannel` resource to update the settings of the Baidu channel for an application. [AWS::Pinpoint::Campaign](aws-resource-pinpoint-campaign.md "aws-resource-pinpoint-campaign.md") Use the `AWS::Pinpoint::Campaign` resource to update the settings for a campaign. [AWS::Pinpoint::EmailChannel](aws-resource-pinpoint-emailchannel.md "aws-resource-pinpoint-emailchannel.md") Use the `AWS::Pinpoint::EmailChannel` resource to update the status and settings of the email channel for an application. [AWS::Pinpoint::EventStream](aws-resource-pinpoint-eventstream.md "aws-resource-pinpoint-eventstream.md") Use the `AWS::Pinpoint::EventStream` resource to create a new event stream for an application or update the settings of an existing event stream for an application. [AWS::Pinpoint::GCMChannel](aws-resource-pinpoint-gcmchannel.md "aws-resource-pinpoint-gcmchannel.md") Use the `AWS::Pinpoint::GCMChannel` resource to specify a GCM channel. You can use the GCM channel to send push notification messages to the Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM) service, which replaced the Google Cloud Messaging (GCM) service. [AWS::Pinpoint::SMSChannel](aws-resource-pinpoint-smschannel.md "aws-resource-pinpoint-smschannel.md") Use the `AWS::Pinpoint::SMSChannel` resource to specify an SMS channel. To send an SMS text message, you send the message through the SMS channel. [AWS::Pinpoint::Segment](aws-resource-pinpoint-segment.md "aws-resource-pinpoint-segment.md") Use the `AWS::Pinpoint::Segment` resource to create a new segment for an application or update the configuration, dimension, and other settings for an existing segment that's associated with an application. [AWS::Pinpoint::VoiceChannel](aws-resource-pinpoint-voicechannel.md "aws-resource-pinpoint-voicechannel.md") Use the `AWS::Pinpoint::VoiceChannel` resource to update the status and settings of the voice channel for an application. [AWS::SageMaker::CodeRepository](aws-resource-sagemaker-coderepository.md "aws-resource-sagemaker-coderepository.md") Use the `AWS::SageMaker::CodeRepository` resource to specify a Git repository as a resource in your SageMaker AI account. | New resources                                                                                                                                                                                                      | The following resources were added: `AWS::Backup::BackupPlan`, `AWS::Backup::BackupSelection`, `AWS::Backup::BackupVault`, `AWS::PinpointEmail::ConfigurationSet`, `AWS::PinpointEmail::ConfigurationSetEventDestination`, `AWS::PinpointEmail::DedicatedIpPool`, `AWS::PinpointEmail::Identity`, `AWS::Transfer::Server`, `AWS::Transfer::User`, `AWS::WAFRegional::GeoMatchSet`, `AWS::WAFRegional::RateBasedRule`, and `AWS::WAFRegional::RegexPatternSet`. [AWS::Backup::BackupPlan](aws-resource-backup-backupplan.md "aws-resource-backup-backupplan.md") Contains an optional backup plan display name and an array of BackupRule objects, each of which specifies a backup rule. Each rule in a backup plan is a separate scheduled task and can back up a different selection of AWS resources. [AWS::Backup::BackupSelection](aws-resource-backup-backupselection.md "aws-resource-backup-backupselection.md") Specifies a set of resources to assign to a backup plan. [AWS::Backup::BackupVault](aws-resource-backup-backupvault.md "aws-resource-backup-backupvault.md") Creates a logical container where backups are stored. A CreateBackupVault request includes a name, optionally one or more resource tags, an encryption key, and a request ID. [AWS::PinpointEmail::ConfigurationSet](aws-resource-pinpointemail-configurationset.md "aws-resource-pinpointemail-configurationset.md") Use the `AWS::PinpointEmail::ConfigurationSet` resource to specify configuration sets for the Amazon Pinpoint Email API. [AWS::PinpointEmail::ConfigurationSetEventDestination](aws-resource-pinpointemail-configurationseteventdestination.md "aws-resource-pinpointemail-configurationseteventdestination.md") Use the `AWS::PinpointEmail::ConfigurationSetEventDestination` resource to specify destinations for events related to sending email in the Amazon Pinpoint Email API. [AWS::PinpointEmail::DedicatedIpPool](aws-resource-pinpointemail-dedicatedippool.md "aws-resource-pinpointemail-dedicatedippool.md") Use the `AWS::PinpointEmail::DedicatedIpPool` resource to specify groups of dedicated IP addresses in the Amazon Pinpoint Email API. [AWS::PinpointEmail::Identity](aws-resource-pinpointemail-identity.md "aws-resource-pinpointemail-identity.md") Use the `AWS::PinpointEmail::Identity` resource to specify identities (email addresses or domains) for sending email through the Amazon Pinpoint Email API. [AWS::Transfer::Server](aws-resource-transfer-server.md "aws-resource-transfer-server.md") Creates an autoscaling virtual server based on Secure File Transfer Protocol (SFTP) in AWS. [AWS::Transfer::User](aws-resource-transfer-user.md "aws-resource-transfer-user.md") Creates a user and associates them with an existing Secure File Transfer Protocol (SFTP) server. [AWS::WafRegional::GeoMatchSet](aws-resource-wafregional-geomatchset.md "aws-resource-wafregional-geomatchset.md") The `AWS::WAFRegional::GeoMatchSet` resource contains one or more countries that AWS WAF will search for. [AWS::WafRegional::RateBasedRule](aws-resource-wafregional-ratebasedrule.md "aws-resource-wafregional-ratebasedrule.md") The `AWS::WAFRegional::RateBasedRule` resource is identical to a regular Rule, with one addition: a RateBasedRule counts the number of requests that arrive from a specified IP address every 5 minutes. [AWS::WafRegional::RegexPatternSet](aws-resource-wafregional-regexpatternset.md "aws-resource-wafregional-regexpatternset.md") The `AWS::WAFRegional::RegexPatternSet` resource specifies the regular expression (regex) pattern that you want AWS WAF to search for. [AWS::AppSync::GraphQLApi](aws-resource-appsync-graphqlapi.md "aws-resource-appsync-graphqlapi.md") Use the `AdditionalAuthenticationProviders` property to specify a list of additional authentication providers for the GraphqlApi API. Use the `Tags` property to specify an arbitrary set of tags (key-value pairs) for this GraphQL API. [AWS::Cognito::UserPool](aws-resource-cognito-userpool.md "aws-resource-cognito-userpool.md") In the [PasswordPolicy](aws-properties-cognito-userpool-passwordpolicy.md "aws-properties-cognito-userpool-passwordpolicy.md") property type, use the `TemporaryPasswordValidityDays` property to specify the number of days a temporary password is valid. If the user does not sign-in during this time, their password will need to be reset by an administrator. NoteWhen you set `TemporaryPasswordValidityDays` for a user pool, you will no longer be able to set the deprecated `UnusedAccountValidityDays` value for that user pool. [AWS::Glue::Classifier](aws-resource-glue-classifier.md "aws-resource-glue-classifier.md") Use the `CsvClassifier` property to specify a classifier for comma-separated values (CSV). [AWS::Glue::Crawler](aws-resource-glue-crawler.md "aws-resource-glue-crawler.md") Use the `CrawlerSecurityConfiguration` property to specify the name of the `SecurityConfiguration` structure to be used by this crawler. Use the `Tags` property to specify the tags to use with this crawler request. You can use tags to limit access to the crawler. [AWS::Glue::DevEndpoint](aws-resource-glue-devendpoint.md "aws-resource-glue-devendpoint.md") Use the `SecurityConfiguration` property to specify the name of the `SecurityConfiguration` structure to be used by this `DevEndpoint`. Use the `Tags` property to specify the tags to use with this `DevEndpoint`. You can use tags to limit access to the `DevEndpoint`. [AWS::Glue::Job](aws-resource-glue-job.md "aws-resource-glue-job.md") Use the `SecurityConfiguration` property to specify the name of the `SecurityConfiguration` structure to be used with this job. Use the `Tags` property to specify the tags to use with this job. You can use tags to limit access to the job. [AWS::Glue::Trigger](aws-resource-glue-trigger.md "aws-resource-glue-trigger.md") Use the `Tags` property to specify the tags to use with this trigger. You can use tags to limit access to the trigger.
